teile.einleitung: The Federal Roads Office, FEDRO for short (in German ASTRA), is responsible for Switzerland's motorways. It plans, builds and maintains the national roads, on which a great many cars and lorries travel every day. It also makes rules for road traffic and vehicles.
wichtigste: FEDRO is the Federal Roads Office and belongs to the department DETEC.
It owns and runs the national roads, that is, the motorways and expressways.
In 1958 the people and the cantons approved the constitutional article on national roads.
In 1962 the Grauholz motorway near Bern opened as the first section of the N1.
FEDRO is based in Ittigen near Bern.
It also deals with traffic rules, vehicle regulations and road safety.
Anyone driving on Swiss motorways needs a vignette.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Roads Office** was founded in 1998 and is part of the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications. It is based in Ittigen on the edge of the city of Bern. It is responsible for the **national roads**, that is, the network of motorways and important expressways. Since 2008 these roads have belonged entirely to the federal government and no longer to the cantons.

In 1958 the people and the cantons voted yes to a constitutional article on national roads. After that, a whole motorway network was planned. The first section of the national road N1, the **Grauholz motorway** near Bern, opened in 1962. Many more stretches were added later, including the Gotthard road tunnel, almost 17 kilometres long, in 1980.

The national road network has several thousand kilometres of carriageway and many tunnels and bridges. FEDRO has damaged road surfaces renewed, tunnels refurbished and bottlenecks widened. A big project is the **second bore** at the Gotthard, so that the old tunnel can be refurbished later. This is paid for, among other things, with money from the vignette and the mineral oil tax on petrol and diesel.

FEDRO draws up the **traffic rules** that apply to all roads. It also decides which regulations apply to cars, bicycles or e-scooters. This includes the Via sicura programme, with which the federal government wants to reduce the number of road deaths. FEDRO also collects figures on accidents in order to identify dangerous spots.

Anyone who drives a car on a Swiss motorway needs a **vignette**. It costs 40 francs a year and, since 2023, can also be bought electronically. Traffic management centres watch the traffic round the clock. When there are jams or accidents, they can change speed limits or close lanes.

begriffe.erklaerung: A road that belongs to the federal government, for example a motorway.
A yearly charge that allows you to use the motorways.
Changes to the constitution need a majority of voters and a majority of the cantons.
A single tunnel through which the carriageway runs.

gewusst: The very first stretch of motorway in Switzerland was already in use near Lucerne in 1955 but was not yet part of the national road network.
When it opened in 1980, the Gotthard road tunnel was the longest road tunnel in the world.
FEDRO is also responsible for the rules on how to get a driving licence in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Supreme Court is the highest court in Switzerland. Its headquarters is in Lausanne, and it is the last body to decide on disputes from all over Switzerland. Its judgements are very important, because all other courts follow them.
wichtigste: The Federal Supreme Court is Switzerland's highest judicial authority.
Its headquarters is in Lausanne, and it has a branch in Lucerne.
Since the total revision of the Federal Constitution in 1874, it has been a permanent court based in Lausanne.
The judges are elected by the United Federal Assembly.
Together with Parliament and the government, it forms the three powers of the state.
It cannot strike down federal laws for being unconstitutional.
In 1990 it ruled that Appenzell Innerrhoden had to introduce votes for women.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Supreme Court** is the highest instance of the Swiss justice system. If someone does not agree with a judgement of a cantonal court or another federal court, they can often turn to it. The Federal Supreme Court then checks whether the law was applied correctly. Its decisions are final and serve as a guide for all other courts.

The headquarters is in the Mon-Repos park in **Lausanne**. There was already a Federal Supreme Court under the Federal Constitution of 1848, but it only met from time to time. With the total revision of the constitution in 1874 it became a permanent court, and in 1875 it was given its seat in Lausanne. In **Lucerne** there are also two divisions that deal with social insurance such as the AVS or disability insurance.

About 40 full-time judges and part-time members work at the Federal Supreme Court. They are elected by the **United Federal Assembly** for six years and can be re-elected. In the election, care is taken that language regions and parties are fairly represented. Judgements are written in German, French or Italian.

In Switzerland there are three powers: making laws, governing and the courts. This is called the **separation of powers**. The Federal Supreme Court is at the very top of the courts. One special feature is that it cannot strike down federal laws for being unconstitutional, because Parliament and the people have the last word here.

Since 1971 women in Switzerland have been able to vote and stand for election at federal level. In the canton of **Appenzell Innerrhoden**, however, women were still not allowed to have a say in cantonal matters even after that. In 1990 the Federal Supreme Court ruled that this breached the equal rights in the Federal Constitution. So the women there gained the cantonal right to vote through a court judgement.

begriffe.erklaerung: A level in the court system that decides on a case.
Dividing the power in the state between Parliament, government and courts.
A court's decision in a dispute.
A complete reworking, for example of the whole constitution.

gewusst: The Federal Supreme Court decides on several thousand cases every year.
The judgements of the Federal Supreme Court are freely available to everyone on the internet.
Part of the Federal Supreme Court used to sit in Lucerne as a separate Federal Insurance Court until the two were merged in 2007.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Communications, OFCOM for short (in German BAKOM), looks after radio, television, telephone, mobile phones and the internet in Switzerland. It makes sure that everyone in the country can communicate well. Without its work, radio signals, for example, would interfere with each other.
wichtigste: OFCOM is a federal office in the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC).
It is based in Biel/Bienne in the canton of Bern.
It regulates radio and television in Switzerland.
It manages the radio frequencies that mobile phones, radios and Wi-Fi need.
It is responsible for Swiss telephone numbers and the internet ending .ch.
It makes sure that emergency numbers such as 112, 117, 118 and 144 work everywhere.
It supervises the collection of the radio and television fee.

abschnitte.text: OFCOM is a specialist office of the **federal administration**. It belongs to the department DETEC, which is headed by a member of the Federal Council. Its headquarters is in Biel/Bienne, a bilingual town on Lake Biel. The office prepares laws, grants licences and checks that the rules are followed. Important foundations are the **Telecommunications Act** and the Radio and Television Act.

OFCOM makes sure that there are radio and television programmes in all parts of the country. SRG SSR receives a **licence** from the Federal Council, that is, permission with a mission, to broadcast programmes in all the national languages. Many local radio stations and regional television channels also receive licences and money from the fee. Every household in Switzerland pays a **radio and television fee**, which is collected by the company Serafe. OFCOM supervises this system.

Mobile phones, radios, Wi-Fi, aviation radio and even garage door openers send signals with invisible **radio waves**. Each use needs its own band, a so-called **frequency**. If two devices send on the same frequency, they interfere with each other. That is why OFCOM shares out the frequencies and tracks down interference with measuring vans. The frequencies for the 5G mobile network were allocated to the mobile providers in an auction in 2019.

OFCOM manages Swiss **telephone numbers**, which begin with the country code +41. It is also responsible for the internet ending **.ch**. It also decides which basic services, the so-called universal service, must be offered everywhere in Switzerland. These include a telephone connection and internet access with a minimum speed, even in remote mountain villages. Some of these tasks are carried out together with the Federal Communications Commission ComCom.

OFCOM makes sure that emergency calls always get through, whichever provider you use. The most important numbers are 117 for the police, 118 for the fire brigade, 144 for the ambulance service and the European **emergency number** 112. The number 147 for children and young people in difficulty is also a protected short number. The office also looks after the security of the communication networks. In disasters, telephone and radio should keep working as far as possible.

begriffe.erklaerung: Official permission with a mission, for example to broadcast a radio programme.
A particular band of radio waves on which a device sends and receives.
Telephone and internet services that must be available everywhere in Switzerland.
The law that regulates telephone, mobile phones and the internet in Switzerland.

gewusst: OFCOM has measuring vehicles with which it can track down illegal transmitters and radio interference.
The internet ending .ch stands for Confoederatio Helvetica, the Latin name of Switzerland.
Because Biel/Bienne is bilingual, it is a fitting home for an office that connects all parts of the country.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of Justice and Police, FDJP for short (in German EJPD), is the federal department for law, security and migration. It prepares new laws, works with the police and is responsible for asylum and naturalisation. History was also made here, because Switzerland's first woman Federal Councillor headed this department.
wichtigste: The FDJP is one of the seven federal departments.
It includes the Federal Office of Justice, the Federal Office of Police and the State Secretariat for Migration.
It prepares many important laws, for example in criminal and civil law.
In 1984 Elisabeth Kopp of the FDP was the first woman elected to the Federal Council, and she headed the FDJP.
Under Justice Minister Arnold Koller the Federal Constitution was totally revised; the people approved it in 1999.
In the Second World War, Heinrich Rothmund was head of the police division in the FDJP and shaped the strict refugee policy.

abschnitte.text: The FDJP makes sure that Switzerland has good, clear **laws**. The Federal Office of Justice checks new laws and helps with cooperation with courts abroad. The Federal Office of Police, fedpol for short, fights serious crime together with the cantons. The State Secretariat for Migration decides on asylum applications and residence permits.

The Federal Institute of Metrology, METAS for short, also belongs to the FDJP. It makes sure that units such as the metre, the kilogram and the second are exactly right in Switzerland. This means you can rely on a set of scales in a shop or a petrol pump measuring correctly. There are also bodies such as the Swiss Institute of Comparative Law in Lausanne.

On 2 October 1984 the Federal Assembly elected **Elisabeth Kopp** of the FDP to the Federal Council. She was the first woman in the national government and took over the Department of Justice and Police. At the end of 1988 she came under criticism because she had warned her husband by telephone about investigations into a company. She therefore resigned at the beginning of 1989.

In the 1990s, Federal Councillor **Arnold Koller** of the CVP, as Justice Minister, led the total revision of the Federal Constitution. The old constitution of 1874 had become confusing because of many changes. On 18 April 1999 the people and the cantons approved the new constitution. It came into force on 1 January 2000 and still applies today.

During the Second World War, **Heinrich Rothmund** was head of the police division in the FDJP and so responsible for the aliens police. He followed a very strict policy towards refugees. In 1938, at Switzerland's request, the so-called **J stamp** was introduced in the passports of German Jews. Many people were turned away at the border, which Switzerland later acknowledged as a grave injustice.

The FDJP has had many well-known heads. They include Christoph Blocher from 2004 to 2007 and Karin Keller-Sutter from 2019 to 2022. Since 2024 **Beat Jans** of the SP has headed the department. Because migration and security are often controversial, the FDJP is frequently in the public eye.

begriffe.erklaerung: A constitution or law is completely rewritten, not just changed in a few places.
The abbreviation for the Federal Office of Police.
The science of precise measurement.
Protection that a state gives to people who are persecuted in their home country.

gewusst: Swiss women only got the right to vote and stand for election at federal level in 1971, just 13 years before the first woman Federal Councillor was elected.
The Federal Institute of Metrology keeps standards against which all important units of measurement in Switzerland are checked.

teile.einleitung: The town and municipal police is the police force of a single town or municipality. In Switzerland the police is mainly a matter for the cantons, but some larger towns also have their own police. The best known is the Zurich City Police.
wichtigste: In Switzerland the cantons are mainly responsible for the police.
Some towns and municipalities also have their own police.
The largest town police force in Switzerland is the Zurich City Police.
The town police deals especially with safety, order and traffic in the town.
It works closely with the cantonal police.
In an emergency you can reach the police on 117.
Many towns have now merged their police with the cantonal police.

abschnitte.text: A town or **municipal police** does not belong to the canton but to a town or municipality. It makes sure that life together in the place is safe and orderly. Its police officers patrol the neighbourhoods on foot, by bike or by car. For serious crimes the **cantonal police** is usually responsible, and the town police works with it.

The **Zurich City Police** is the largest municipal police force in Switzerland. Winterthur and St Gallen also have their own town police. In French-speaking Switzerland there is, for example, the police of the city of Lausanne, and in Ticino the police of the city of Lugano. In Bern and Lucerne, on the other hand, the town police has been merged with the cantonal police.

The town police directs **traffic**, checks parking and looks after safety at events. It deals with noise complaints, for example when a party is too loud in the middle of the night. It also helps at accidents, searches for missing people and takes down reports of crimes. At large events such as football matches or demonstrations, it is out in force.

Many town police forces visit schools and teach children about **road safety**. In a traffic training ground, for example, children practise how to behave on a bike and when crossing the road. Topics such as safety on the internet are also discussed at school. If you need help, you can turn to a police officer at any time.

The police may, for example, ask to see an identity document or check people, but in doing so it must keep to the **law**. It must treat everyone fairly and with respect. In an emergency you dial 117, which goes to the responsible control centre. For matters that are not urgent there are police stations in the neighbourhoods.

begriffe.erklaerung: Police that belongs to a town or municipality and keeps order there.
The police of a canton, which bears the main responsibility in Switzerland.
Police officers who walk or drive through an area to check it.
Informing the police that a crime has probably taken place.

gewusst: The Zurich City Police is responsible for a city with more than 400,000 inhabitants.
Many small municipalities have no police of their own; there the cantonal police takes on all the tasks.
Many police officers in Swiss towns also go on patrol by bike.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of Home Affairs, FDHA for short (in German EDI), is one of the seven departments of the Swiss federal administration. It deals with topics that affect the lives of almost everyone, for example health, pensions and culture. It is headed by a member of the Federal Council.
wichtigste: The FDHA is one of the seven federal departments.
Since 2024 it has been headed by Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider.
It is responsible for health, social insurance and culture.
The FDHA includes, among others, the Federal Office of Public Health and the Federal Social Insurance Office.
The Federal Statistical Office and MeteoSwiss also belong to it.
The National Library and the Swiss National Museum are part of the FDHA.
Because of the AVS, the FDHA manages a very large part of the federal budget.

abschnitte.text: The **Department of Home Affairs** is one of the seven large parts of the federal administration. Each department is led by a member of the Federal Council. Since 2024 Elisabeth Baume-Schneider has headed the FDHA. Its headquarters is in the Federal Palace in Bern.

The **Federal Office of Public Health**, FOPH for short, belongs to the FDHA. It deals with health insurance, vaccinations and fighting diseases. During the coronavirus pandemic the FOPH was in the news especially often. The Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office also makes sure that food is safe and animals stay healthy.

The **Federal Social Insurance Office** is responsible for the AVS, disability insurance and other insurance schemes. The **AVS** pays older people a pension, and disability insurance helps people with a disability. Because the federal government pays a lot of money into these insurance schemes, the FDHA is one of the departments with the largest spending. Family allowances are also among its topics.

The **Federal Office of Culture** supports film, art, music, literature and the protection of monuments. The Swiss National Library in Bern and the Swiss National Museum with the National Museum in Zurich also belong to the FDHA. The office also supports the national languages, for example Romansh. In this way Switzerland's cultural diversity is cared for.

**MeteoSwiss**, the federal weather service, also belongs to the FDHA. It makes weather forecasts and warns of severe weather, heat or storms. The Federal Statistical Office in Neuchâtel collects figures on the population and the economy. In addition, a separate office works for equality between women and men.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large area of the federal administration headed by a member of the Federal Council.
Old-age and survivors' insurance, which pays pensions to older people.
Insurance that protects people in difficult situations in life.
A specialist office within a department.

gewusst: The weather warnings in the MeteoSwiss app come from an office of the FDHA.
The National Library keeps a copy of almost every book published in Switzerland.
The FDHA is responsible for things as different as health insurance funds, museums and weather forecasts.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH, in German BAG) is the federal government's most important health authority. It protects the population from diseases, issues vaccination recommendations and supervises health insurance. Many people got to know it during the coronavirus pandemic.
wichtigste: The FOPH belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and is based in Bern.
It publishes the official Swiss vaccination schedule.
The FOPH supervises compulsory health insurance and approves the premiums.
According to the FOPH, all cantons except Ticino count as risk areas for the tick-borne disease TBE.
The TBE vaccination is generally recommended from the age of 3.
The most common tick-borne disease in Switzerland is Lyme disease.
The FOPH also deals with radiation protection, chemicals and addiction prevention.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Public Health** is a federal authority based in Bern. It belongs to the **Federal Department of Home Affairs** (FDHA). Together with the cantons, it looks after the health of the population. The FOPH prepares laws, monitors infectious diseases and informs the public. The hospitals and doctors' surgeries themselves, on the other hand, are mainly a matter for the cantons.

Together with an expert commission, the FOPH publishes the official **Swiss vaccination schedule**. It says which vaccinations are recommended at which age. Doctors must report certain infectious diseases to the FOPH so that outbreaks are noticed early. During the **coronavirus pandemic** from 2020, the FOPH published figures and protective rules every day. Campaigns on flu, measles or AIDS also come from the FOPH.

Ticks can pass on dangerous diseases, most often **Lyme disease**. The disease **TBE**, an inflammation of the brain and its membranes caused by viruses, can be prevented with a vaccination. According to the FOPH, all cantons except Ticino count as TBE risk areas, and the vaccination is generally recommended from the age of 3. In the woods you should stay on wide paths, avoid undergrowth and check your body for ticks afterwards. The free app “Zecke”, developed at ZHAW with the support of the FOPH, helps with this.

In Switzerland everyone must take out **basic insurance** with a health insurance fund. The FOPH supervises this insurance and approves the **premiums** every year. It also decides which treatments and medicines the basic insurance must pay for. The new premiums for the following year are announced each autumn. They are an important topic in many families.

The FOPH also deals with **radiation protection**, for example in X-rays or with the radioactive gas radon in basements. It regulates the handling of dangerous **chemicals**. Another area is the prevention of addiction, for example to alcohol, tobacco or drugs. Campaigns are meant to help people live healthily. The FOPH also works with the World Health Organization WHO, which has its headquarters in Geneva.

begriffe.erklaerung: A list of which vaccinations are recommended at which age.
Tick-borne encephalitis, a viral inflammation of the brain passed on by ticks.
The amount you pay regularly to the health insurance fund.
Measures that prevent diseases before they arise.

gewusst: Ticks do not jump from trees; they usually wait on grass and bushes for people and animals to brush past.
There is no vaccination against Lyme disease, but there is one against TBE.
The World Health Organization WHO has its headquarters in Geneva.

teile.einleitung: The State Secretariat for Migration, SEM for short, is the federal authority for all questions about immigration, asylum and naturalisation. It decides, for example, whether a refugee receives protection in Switzerland. It also regulates who may enter Switzerland and work and live here.
wichtigste: The SEM belongs to the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
It has had this name since 2015; before that it was called the Federal Office for Migration.
It decides on asylum applications in Switzerland.
It runs federal asylum centres, where asylum seekers live during the procedure.
Together with the cantons, it regulates the residence, work and naturalisation of foreign nationals.
In 2022 Switzerland activated protection status S for the first time, for refugees from Ukraine.

abschnitte.text: The SEM has its headquarters in Wabern near Bern. It was created in 2005 as the **Federal Office for Migration** from two earlier offices and was upgraded to a state secretariat on 1 January 2015. It is responsible for **migration**, that is, for people who move to Switzerland or seek protection here. It works closely with the cantons, which are responsible for many practical matters.

People who are persecuted in their home country can make an **asylum application** in Switzerland. Since 2019 most applications have been examined in an accelerated procedure in federal asylum centres. Asylum seekers receive free legal representation during this. Those recognised as refugees may stay; those who have no right to protection must usually leave Switzerland.

Foreign nationals in Switzerland need a **residence permit**. There are different permits, for example permit B for residence, permit C for settlement or permit G for cross-border commuters. For people from EU and EFTA states, the free movement of persons has applied since 2002, which makes it easier to work in Switzerland. The foreign share of the population is about a quarter (as of about 2024).

In March 2022 the Federal Council activated **protection status S** for the first time. It was intended for people fleeing the war in Ukraine. With this status, people seeking protection receive it quickly and without a long asylum procedure. Tens of thousands of people from Ukraine came to Switzerland in this way.

Anyone who wants to become Swiss needs the approval of the federal government, the canton and the municipality for **naturalisation**. The SEM grants the federal approval. It also supports **integration**, for example with language courses that it promotes together with the cantons. The SEM also works with other European countries within the framework of Schengen and Dublin.

begriffe.erklaerung: When people move their home permanently to another country or region.
Protection that a state gives to people who are persecuted in their home country.
The process by which a foreign person obtains Swiss citizenship.
Growing into a new society, for example through language, work and friendships.

gewusst: For ordinary naturalisation you usually have to have lived in Switzerland for at least ten years.
Switzerland has taken part in Schengen and Dublin since 2008, even though it is not a member of the EU.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Armed Forces protect the country and its population and help in disasters. They are a militia army: most soldiers have a normal job and serve for only a few weeks a year. In this way Switzerland defends its neutrality with its own means.
wichtigste: The Swiss Armed Forces are a militia army; most of their members are not professional soldiers.
Swiss men have to do military service, and women can serve voluntarily.
Their tasks are defence, supporting the civil authorities and promoting peace.
Switzerland practises armed neutrality: it defends its neutrality with its own army.
A general is elected by the Federal Assembly only in times of great threat or war.
In the Second World War, Henri Guisan was commander-in-chief of the army.
Since 1999 the Swiss contingent Swisscoy has served in KFOR in Kosovo.

abschnitte.text: The Swiss Armed Forces are based on the **militia principle**. Young men first attend recruit school, which usually lasts 18 weeks, and then several refresher courses. Anyone who cannot do military service for reasons of conscience can do civilian service, and those who are unfit often go into civil defence. The army's target strength is 100,000 members. It is led by the Chief of the Armed Forces, and political responsibility lies with the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).

The main task is the **defence** of the country and its airspace. For this, the air force watches over the Swiss sky round the clock. The army also supports civil authorities, for example in floods, avalanches, during the coronavirus pandemic or in protecting the World Economic Forum in Davos. It also contributes to international **peace promotion**.

In peacetime the Swiss Armed Forces have no general. Only in times of great threat or war does the **Federal Assembly** elect a general as commander-in-chief. In 1815, during Napoleon's Hundred Days, Niklaus Franz von Bachmann led the federal army, which briefly advanced into the Franche-Comté. On 3 August 1914, at the start of the First World War, Ulrich Wille was elected general.

abschnitte.titel: The Second World War and the Réduit
abschnitte.text: On 30 August 1939, shortly before the war began, the Federal Assembly elected **Henri Guisan** as general. Guisan came from Vaud and had been a farmer before his military career. On 2 September 1939 general mobilisation for war began. In summer 1940 Guisan gathered the officers on the Rütli meadow and presented the **Réduit**, a plan in which the army would withdraw into the Alps and defend itself there.

Since 1953 Switzerland has been a member of the Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission, the **NNSC**, in Panmunjom on the border between North and South Korea. Since 1999 the **Swisscoy** contingent has served in the international peacekeeping force KFOR in Kosovo. Swiss military observers also serve in UN missions around the world. These missions are voluntary.

A world-famous symbol of the army is the **Swiss Army knife**. At the end of 1891 the cutler Karl Elsener from Ibach in the canton of Schwyz took over making soldiers' knives for the army. His workshop later became the company Victorinox. The red pocket knife with the Swiss cross is known all over the world today.

begriffe.erklaerung: A system in which citizens take on tasks for the state alongside their jobs.
The first basic military training that young men in Switzerland complete.
A defence plan in the Second World War in which the army was to withdraw into the Alps.
A country does not take part in wars between other states.
All soldiers are called up so that the army is ready for action.

gewusst: In the history of the federal state there have been only four generals: Guillaume-Henri Dufour, Hans Herzog, Ulrich Wille and Henri Guisan.
In 1989 more than a third of voters supported an initiative that wanted to abolish the army completely.
Many members of the army keep their personal weapon at home, which is very unusual in other countries.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss National Bank, SNB for short, is Switzerland's central bank. It issues the banknotes, sets the key interest rate and makes sure that the franc keeps its value. It is independent of the Federal Council but must act for the good of the whole country.
wichtigste: The SNB issues Swiss banknotes.
Its most important legal goal is to ensure price stability.
Price stability means inflation of less than 2 per cent a year.
With the key interest rate, it steers the economy and keeps prices stable.
It began business in 1907 and has offices in Bern and Zurich.
From 2011 to January 2015 it defended a minimum exchange rate of 1.20 francs to the euro.
One third of its ordinary profit goes to the federal government and two thirds to the cantons.

abschnitte.text: A **central bank** is the bank of the banks and of the state. Private individuals cannot open an account at the SNB. The SNB supplies the economy with money, manages Switzerland's currency reserves and helps to keep the banking system stable. It is led by a three-member **Governing Board**, headed by the Chairman.

The SNB prints and distributes all franc **banknotes**, while the coins are minted by Swissmint on behalf of the federal government. From 2016 to 2019 it issued the ninth series of banknotes, ranging from 10 to 1000 francs. Each note shows a typical characteristic of Switzerland, such as its talent for organisation or its humanitarian tradition. The notes have many security features so that they can hardly be forged.

abschnitte.titel: Key interest rate and price stability
abschnitte.text: The SNB sets the **key interest rate**. If it lowers the rate, borrowing money becomes cheaper and the economy is boosted. If it raises it, this slows down the economy and so also rising prices. The aim is to keep **inflation** below 2 per cent a year, so that a franc tomorrow is worth almost as much as today.

The National Bank Act came into force in 1906, and on 20 June 1907 the SNB began its work. Before that, many different banks issued their own banknotes. According to the **Bergier Commission**, during the Second World War the SNB bought gold worth about 1.2 billion francs from the German Reichsbank, including looted gold. This was later strongly criticised.

In the financial crisis of October 2008, the federal government and the National Bank supported the big bank **UBS**. The SNB took over UBS's problem securities into a special-purpose company called StabFund. Because the franc became very strong, in 2011 the SNB set a **minimum exchange rate** of 1.20 francs to the euro and surprisingly lifted it again in January 2015. In March 2023 the SNB helped with a lot of money when UBS took over the troubled Credit Suisse.

The SNB is a **public limited company** whose shares are traded on the stock exchange. However, most of the shares belong to cantons and cantonal banks. Under an agreement with the federal government, its profit goes to the public sector. The federal government receives one third and the cantons two thirds.

begriffe.erklaerung: A country's top bank, which issues the money and makes monetary policy.
The interest rate the National Bank uses to steer how expensive it is to borrow money.
When prices for goods and services rise on average.
A limit below which the value of a currency should not fall.
Gold and foreign money that the National Bank holds as a reserve.

gewusst: The SNB owns more than 1000 tonnes of gold, some of which is stored abroad.
From 2015 to 2022 Switzerland had a negative key interest rate, so banks had to pay for certain deposits at the SNB.
Switzerland's 1000-franc note is one of the most valuable banknotes in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Administrative Court, FAC for short (in German BVGer), is the largest federal court and is in St Gallen. It checks whether decisions of the federal administration are lawful. Anyone who disagrees with a decision of a federal office can often turn to it.
wichtigste: The Federal Administrative Court is in St Gallen.
It began its work in 2007 and moved to St Gallen in 2012.
It is the largest federal court.
It reviews rulings by federal authorities, for example by federal offices.
A large share of its cases concern asylum law.
In many areas its judgements can be challenged at the Federal Supreme Court.
In asylum decisions it usually has the final say.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Administrative Court** is a court that judges disputes with the federal administration. When a federal office issues a ruling, that is, a binding decision, you can lodge an appeal against it. The court then checks whether the authority acted correctly. In this way it protects people from the state deciding unfairly.

The court opened on 1 January 2007 and replaced more than 30 separate appeals commissions. At first it worked temporarily in Bern and Zollikofen. In 2012 it moved into a new building in **St Gallen**. This gave eastern Switzerland an important federal court too.

The FAC judges cases from many areas. These include asylum and the law on foreign nationals, federal taxes, social insurance, the environment, transport and public contracts. A large share of the cases concern **asylum law**, that is, decisions by the State Secretariat for Migration. Disputes about admission to study medicine or about radio licences can also end up here.

About 70 judges work at the court, divided among several **divisions**. They are elected by the United Federal Assembly for six years. They are supported by numerous court clerks, who prepare the judgements. Work is done in German, French and Italian.

In many areas a judgement of the FAC can still be challenged at the **Federal Supreme Court** in Lausanne. In asylum decisions, however, the Federal Administrative Court is usually the last instance. Its decisions are then final. That is why the court is very important for many people.

begriffe.erklaerung: A binding decision by an authority in an individual case.
A request to have a decision reviewed by a higher body.
Protection that a state grants to people who are persecuted in their home country.
A level in the court system.

gewusst: The Federal Administrative Court deals with several thousand cases every year.
The court building in St Gallen was newly built especially for the Federal Administrative Court.
Before 2007, many of these cases had their own small commissions instead of one large court.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Criminal Court is the federal government's criminal court and is based in Bellinzona in Ticino. It tries especially serious or cross-border crimes for which the federal government is responsible. These include, for example, terrorism or large cases of money laundering.
wichtigste: The Federal Criminal Court is the federal criminal court of first instance.
It is based in Bellinzona in the canton of Ticino.
It began its work in 2004.
The prosecution is brought by the Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland.
It tries cases such as terrorism, explosives offences, counterfeit money and large economic cases.
Its judgements can be taken to the Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne.
However, most crimes in Switzerland are tried by cantonal courts.

abschnitte.titel: What is the Federal Criminal Court?
abschnitte.text: The **Federal Criminal Court** is a court that judges crimes that fall within the responsibility of the federal government. It was created in 2004 to strengthen criminal prosecution in serious and complicated cases. Most offences, such as theft or road accidents, go before the cantonal courts instead. So the Federal Criminal Court is there for special cases.

The court is based in **Bellinzona**, the capital of the canton of Ticino. This makes it the first federal court in Italian-speaking Switzerland. The town is also known for its three castles, which are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. However, the court holds hearings in all the official languages, depending on which language the accused speak.

Cases that come before the Federal Criminal Court include **terrorism**, bomb attacks and aircraft hijackings. Counterfeit money, espionage and crimes against federal authorities also belong here. Large cases of money laundering, corruption and organised crime that affect several cantons or countries are also tried here. The prosecution is brought in each case by the **Office of the Attorney General** in Bern.

The court has several chambers. The Criminal Chamber holds the trials and passes the judgements at first instance. The Appeals Chamber checks, for example, whether an arrest or a house search was lawful. Since 2019 there has also been a **Court of Appeal**, where a judgement of the Criminal Chamber can be reviewed again.

Anyone who does not agree with a decision of the Federal Criminal Court can turn to the **Federal Supreme Court**. It has its headquarters in Lausanne and is Switzerland's highest court. There, it is checked whether the law was applied correctly. In this way there are several levels, so that mistakes can be corrected.

begriffe.erklaerung: A court that decides whether someone has committed a crime and what punishment they receive.
The authority that investigates federal crimes and brings the prosecution.
Moving money from crime in such a way that its origin stays hidden.
The possibility of having a judgement looked at again by a higher court.

gewusst: One reason Bellinzona was chosen as the seat was so that Italian-speaking Switzerland would also have a federal court.
The Federal Criminal Court has far fewer cases than a large cantonal criminal court, but they are often very extensive.
Some trials at the Federal Criminal Court concern money that was brought into Switzerland from abroad.

teile.einleitung: The cantonal police is the police force of a canton. In Switzerland each of the 26 cantons has its own police force, which looks after safety and traffic and solves crimes. In an emergency you can reach the police on 117.
wichtigste: Each canton has its own cantonal police, because in Switzerland the police is a matter for the cantons.
In an emergency you can reach the police on 117 or the European emergency number 112.
The cantonal police keeps people safe and maintains order, directs traffic and solves crimes.
Together with the courts and authorities, it exercises the state's monopoly on the use of force.
Police dogs help, for example, to track down people or drugs.
At large events the cantonal police forces help each other out.

abschnitte.text: Because Switzerland is a **federal state**, the cantons have police sovereignty. That is why there are 26 different cantonal police forces, with their own uniforms, vehicles and laws. Large cantons such as Zurich or Bern have thousands of police officers, small cantons only a few dozen. In some cantons they also work together with town or municipal police forces.

The **security police** patrol, help in emergencies and keep the peace. The **criminal police** investigate theft, fraud or violent crimes and secure evidence at the crime scene. The traffic police check speed and fitness to drive and investigate accidents. Cantons with large lakes also have a lake police.

In a state governed by the rule of law, only the state may lawfully use **force**, for example through the police and the courts. This is called the state's monopoly on the use of force. But the police may only use as much force as is absolutely necessary. Its work is checked by courts, parliaments and the public.

The police use trained **police dogs**, which track down people, drugs or explosives. For crimes across national borders, they work with the Federal Office of Police and, through Interpol, with police forces in other countries. For large events such as football matches or conferences, other cantons send reinforcements; this is arranged by so-called **concordats**. Modern technology such as drones and DNA analysis helps in investigations.

The police has not always been uncontroversial. During the strike by tunnel workers in Göschenen in July 1875, while the Gotthard tunnel was being built, a police troop fired into the crowd. Four workers died. Today much more importance is attached to police operations being proportionate.

Anyone who wants to join the police usually needs a completed apprenticeship or a baccalaureate and must be healthy and fit. Training takes place at a **police school**, for example the Intercantonal Police School in Hitzkirch in the canton of Lucerne. At the end there is a federal professional examination. The job is varied but also requires courage and empathy.

begriffe.erklaerung: A canton's right to run its own police force.
Only the state may lawfully use force, for example through the police and the courts.
The part of the police that solves crimes.
An agreement between several cantons, for example on police cooperation.

gewusst: Police cars look very different depending on the canton; you can tell where they come from by their colours and the cantonal coat of arms.
In Basel-Stadt there is no separate town police; the cantonal police is also responsible for the town there.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Intelligence Service, FIS for short (in German NDB), is Switzerland's secret service. It collects information about dangers such as terrorism, espionage or attacks on computers and warns the government about them. Because its work is secret, it is strictly supervised by several bodies.
wichtigste: The FIS is Switzerland's civilian intelligence service.
It was formed in 2010 from two earlier services and belongs to the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
Its main topics are terrorism, violent extremism, espionage and attacks on the internet.
It informs the Federal Council so that it can make good decisions on security.
Since 2017 the Intelligence Service Act has applied, which voters approved in 2016.
An independent supervisory authority and Parliament supervise the FIS.

abschnitte.text: An **intelligence service** is an authority that collects and analyses information about dangers to a country. It watches, for example, whether foreign states are spying in Switzerland. It looks for signs of planned attacks or of groups that intend to use violence. It passes on its findings to the Federal Council, the army and the police.

The FIS was founded on 1 January 2010. At that time the **Service for Analysis and Prevention**, which dealt with security at home, and the **Strategic Intelligence Service** for abroad were merged. Since then there has been a single civilian intelligence service. It is based in Bern.

Much of the information comes from publicly available sources such as newspapers and the internet. There are also tips from partner services in other countries. With permission, in serious cases the FIS can also tap telephones or search computers. For this, however, it needs the approval of a court and of the head of the DDPS.

The **Intelligence Service Act** sets out what the FIS may and may not do. A referendum was called against the law, and so a popular vote was held on 25 September 2016. About two thirds of voters said yes. The law came into force on 1 September 2017.

abschnitte.titel: Supervision and the secret files scandal
abschnitte.text: In 1989 it came to light that the federal police had for decades kept hundreds of thousands of **secret files**, that is, index cards about people and organisations. This scandal caused great outrage. Since then the work of the intelligence services has been supervised much more strictly. Today an independent **supervisory authority** and Parliament's Control Committee delegation supervise the FIS.

begriffe.erklaerung: An authority that collects secret and public information about dangers to a country.
Secretly finding out the secrets of another country or a company.
An index card on which information about a person was noted.
Political or religious attitudes that reject democracy and the rights of others, often with violence.

gewusst: In the secret files scandal, people affected could see their own file, and hundreds of thousands of people asked to do so.
Every year the FIS publishes a public situation report called “Switzerland's Security”.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for Civil Protection (FOCP, in German BABS) makes sure that people in Switzerland are protected in disasters and emergencies. It looks after sirens, shelters and civil defence. The FOCP is based in Bern.
wichtigste: The FOCP belongs to the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
It prepares Switzerland for disasters such as earthquakes, floods or power cuts.
The FOCP is responsible for the sirens and for alerting the population.
Every year in February, the nationwide siren test takes place.
The National Emergency Operations Centre and the Spiez Laboratory belong to the FOCP.
The Alertswiss app gives information about warnings and alarms.
In Switzerland there is a place in a shelter for almost every inhabitant.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office for Civil Protection** is a federal authority based in Bern. It belongs to the **DDPS**, the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport. Its task is to protect the population from disasters and emergencies. These include natural events such as earthquakes, floods or avalanches, but also power cuts, pandemics or accidents in nuclear power stations. The FOCP works closely with the cantons.

**Civil protection** in Switzerland is a network of five partners. They are the police, the fire brigade, the health services, the technical services and **civil defence**. In a major event they work together under one command. The federal government sets the rules, and the cantons are responsible for the work on the ground. The FOCP looks after training, planning and cooperation.

There are thousands of **sirens** all over Switzerland that warn the population of danger. When the “general alarm” sounds, a wailing tone that rises and falls, you should listen to the radio, follow the instructions and tell your neighbours. Every year on the first Wednesday in February, all sirens are checked in the **siren test**. In addition, the **Alertswiss** app sends warnings straight to your phone. The **National Emergency Operations Centre** in Zurich is staffed round the clock.

Switzerland has a special feature: there is a place in a **shelter** for almost every inhabitant. These rooms are usually in the basement of blocks of flats or in public buildings. They have thick concrete walls, heavy doors and ventilation with filters. Many were built during the Cold War. The FOCP sets out how shelters must be built and maintained.

The **Spiez Laboratory** in the Bernese Oberland belongs to the FOCP. There, experts examine dangerous chemical, biological and radioactive substances. The laboratory is also known internationally and helps, for example, with investigations into chemical weapons. The FOCP also looks after the **protection of cultural property**. This means protecting valuable buildings, works of art and archives from destruction in war or disasters.

begriffe.erklaerung: An organisation in which people doing protection service help in disasters.
An especially safe room, usually in the basement, that gives protection in danger.
The yearly check of all sirens on the first Wednesday in February.
Protecting valuable buildings, works of art and archives.

gewusst: Hardly any other country has as many shelter places for its population as Switzerland.
During the siren test in February, sirens wail all over Switzerland at the same time.
The “water alarm” sounds different from the general alarm and warns of danger from dams.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Topography, swisstopo for short, surveys Switzerland and draws its official maps. It knows exactly where every mountain, every river and every house is. The Swiss maps by swisstopo are thought to be especially beautiful and accurate all over the world.
wichtigste: swisstopo is responsible in Switzerland for the national survey and the official maps.
The office belongs to the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
It is based in Wabern near Bern.
Its roots go back to 1838, when Guillaume-Henri Dufour founded the Topographic Bureau.
Switzerland's highest peak, the Dufourspitze, is named after Dufour.
swisstopo also studies what lies beneath Switzerland's surface, that is, its geology.
All the maps can be viewed free of charge on the internet and in an app.

abschnitte.text: swisstopo is the federal specialist office for **geoinformation**, that is, all information about where something is. It belongs to the DDPS and is based in Wabern, a place in the municipality of Köniz near Bern. The office surveys the country, makes maps, takes aerial photographs and collects data on rock and soil. These data are needed, for example, by civil engineers, authorities, rescue services and hikers. Satnavs and apps also often use data from swisstopo.

In 1838 the Geneva general **Guillaume-Henri Dufour** founded the Federal Topographic Bureau. Under his leadership, the first accurate map of the whole of Switzerland was made at a scale of 1:100,000, the **Dufour map**. The work took many years; the sheets appeared from 1845 into the 1860s. The mountains were drawn on it with shading so that they look almost three-dimensional. In honour of Dufour, Switzerland's highest peak, in the Monte Rosa massif, was named the Dufourspitze; it is 4634 metres high.

For a map to be right, the country must first be surveyed precisely. For this there are thousands of **survey points** all over Switzerland whose position is known to the centimetre. Today satellites also help. Every place in Switzerland has its own **national coordinates**, which you can read off at the edge of every national map. The starting point for heights is a boulder in Lake Geneva, the Repère Pierre du Niton.

The best-known products are the **national maps** at various scales, for example 1:25,000 and 1:50,000. On a map at a scale of 1:25,000, one centimetre corresponds to 250 metres in reality. Typical of Swiss maps are the fine rock drawing and the shading, which make mountains look three-dimensional. The maps are updated regularly so that new roads and houses are shown. Today they can be viewed free of charge on map.geo.admin.ch or in the swisstopo app.

swisstopo is also Switzerland's **national geological survey**. It makes geological maps showing which rocks lie in the ground. In the Mont Terri rock laboratory in the canton of Jura, scientists study how rock behaves over very long periods. In addition, swisstopo aircraft regularly photograph Switzerland from above. This creates a huge archive of **aerial photographs**, in which you can see how villages and landscapes have changed.

begriffe.erklaerung: The description of the Earth's surface with its mountains, valleys, rivers and buildings.
Shows how much smaller a map is compared with reality.
Numbers that let you pinpoint a place on the map exactly.
Precisely measuring the position, size and height of land and buildings.

gewusst: In the past, cartographers secretly hid small drawings in the national maps, for example a marmot or a spider.
The Dufourspitze used to be called the Gornerhorn and got its present name in 1863.
With the swisstopo app you can see on your phone what an area looked like more than a hundred years ago.

teile.einleitung: The military police is the police of the Swiss Armed Forces. It keeps order and security in the army, directs military traffic and investigates crimes committed by members of the army. You can recognise its members by the abbreviation MP.
wichtigste: The military police is the police within the Swiss Armed Forces.
It consists of professionals and of militia members who serve during their military service.
It looks after security, order and traffic in the army.
It investigates when members of the army break military criminal law.
It supports civil authorities, for example at large events or in protecting embassies.
Its members wear the marking “MP” for military police.

abschnitte.text: The **military police** is part of the Swiss Armed Forces. For the army it takes on tasks similar to those the civilian police carry out for the population. Some of its members work all year round as **professional military police**. In addition there are militia units, whose members serve as military police officers during their military service.

During large exercises, many military vehicles move along the roads. The military police then directs the **traffic** and escorts convoys. It checks vehicles and drivers and investigates accidents involving army vehicles. It also guards military sites and makes sure that unauthorised people do not get in.

When a member of the army commits a crime, for example a theft in the barracks, the military police investigates. **Military criminal law** applies to members of the army on duty. The cases are then judged by the **military justice system**, with its own examining magistrates and military courts. In this way the army remains a place where law and order apply.

The military police also helps with operations outside the army. At the World Economic Forum in Davos, the army supports the Grisons cantonal police every year. The military police has also helped to protect foreign **embassies** when the police did not have enough staff. In doing so, it is always under the command of the civil authorities.

Anyone who wants to join the military police must meet special requirements, such as a good reputation and good physical fitness. The training covers law, self-defence, driving vehicles and dealing with people in difficult situations. For the professional military police, a completed apprenticeship is usually needed. Many skills from this training are also in demand in the civilian police.

begriffe.erklaerung: Special laws that apply to members of the army, for example during military service.
The army's courts and investigating authorities.
A system in which citizens take on tasks for the state alongside their jobs.
Several vehicles travelling together one behind the other.

gewusst: In many other countries the military police is also called “MP”, because the abbreviation is the same in English and German.
The military police works closely with the civilian police on many operations, even though it belongs to the army.

teile.einleitung: The transport police looks after safety on public transport in Switzerland. Its officers are out and about on trains and in stations and help travellers in emergencies. It belongs to SBB and is the best-known railway police in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The transport police looks after safety on trains, in stations and on public transport.
It belongs to the Swiss Federal Railways SBB.
Its work is regulated in the Federal Act on the Security Bodies of Transport Companies.
It may, for example, check identity documents and detain people temporarily.
It hands serious crimes over to the cantonal police.
It is also on duty at large events such as football matches, when many fans travel by train.
Anyone threatened on a train can get help on the emergency number 117.

abschnitte.text: The **transport police** is a police force especially for public transport. In Switzerland this mainly means the **SBB** transport police. Its staff wear uniform and are out and about on trains, on platforms and in stations. They make sure that travellers and staff feel safe.

The work of the transport police is regulated in the **Federal Act on the Security Bodies of Transport Companies**, which has applied since 2011. It sets out what the transport police may and may not do. Unlike the cantonal police, it is only responsible for public transport. It works on behalf of SBB and also for other rail and bus companies.

The transport police steps in when there is a quarrel on the train or someone is bothering other passengers. It deals with **vandalism**, for example when seats are slashed or carriages are sprayed with graffiti. It checks people who are travelling without a ticket and refuse to identify themselves. It also escorts special trains carrying **football fans** and helps to direct crowds at large events.

The transport police works closely with the **cantonal police forces** and the town police forces. When it detains someone who has committed a crime, it hands the person over to the responsible police. It is supported by security staff from the company Securitrans, who keep order at stations. In this way a dense network for safety on public transport is created.

If you feel threatened on the train, sit near other travellers or the train staff. Many trains have an **emergency intercom** or an emergency brake for real emergencies. In an emergency you can call the police on 117 at any time. The train staff can also quickly alert the transport police by radio.

begriffe.erklaerung: Police responsible for safety on trains and in stations.
Swiss Federal Railways, the largest railway company in Switzerland.
When someone deliberately breaks or defaces other people's property.
The place in a station where you get on the train; in Switzerland called “Perron”.

gewusst: The transport police sometimes escorts whole special trains in which only football fans are travelling.
The transport police can also work with other rail and bus companies, not just with SBB.
Switzerland has one of the densest railway networks in the world, which is why safety on trains is especially important.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, FDFA for short (in German EDA), is responsible for Switzerland's foreign policy. It looks after relations with other countries and international organisations. It also helps Swiss citizens who get into difficulties abroad.
wichtigste: The FDFA is the department for Switzerland's foreign policy.
It looks after relations with other countries.
Since 2017 it has been headed by Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis.
Switzerland has about 170 embassies, consulates and other representations around the world.
The Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) belongs to the FDFA.
The SDC supports projects in poorer countries.
With its good offices, Switzerland often mediates between states in conflict.

abschnitte.text: The **Department of Foreign Affairs** is one of the seven federal departments. It is responsible for **foreign policy**, that is, Switzerland's relations with other countries. Its headquarters is in the West Wing of the Federal Palace in Bern. Since 2017 Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis has headed the FDFA.

Switzerland has about 170 representations all over the world, including **embassies** and consulates. An embassy represents Switzerland to the government of another country. Diplomats there negotiate, for example, about trade, the environment or cooperation. Consulates help Swiss citizens who live or travel abroad.

Switzerland is a **neutral** country and does not take part in wars between other states. With its **good offices**, it offers to mediate between parties in a conflict or to organise meetings. Sometimes it acts as a protecting power, representing one country's interests in another, for example the interests of the USA in Iran since 1980. Peace talks are often held in Geneva, where many international organisations are based.

The **SDC**, the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, belongs to the FDFA. It supports projects in poorer countries, for example for clean water, schools or agriculture. After earthquakes, floods or wars, the federal government's humanitarian aid helps. This includes the Swiss Humanitarian Aid Unit, with experts who can set off quickly.

Switzerland has been a member of the **UN** since 2002, after the people voted to join. In 2023 and 2024 it sat on the UN Security Council for the first time. The FDFA also negotiates relations with the European Union, Switzerland's most important trading partner. Anyone travelling abroad can find travel advice from the FDFA with safety information on many countries.

begriffe.erklaerung: How a state shapes its relations with other states.
The official representation of one country in another country.
A state does not take part in other states' wars.
Offers by Switzerland to mediate between parties in a dispute.
A person who represents their country abroad and negotiates.

gewusst: Geneva is one of the most important UN locations outside New York.
The FDFA runs a helpline that Swiss travellers can call round the clock in an emergency.
Switzerland only joined the UN in 2002, much later than most other countries.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for the Environment, FOEN for short (in German BAFU), looks after nature and the environment in Switzerland. It works for clean water, healthy air, healthy forests and many animal and plant species. It also helps to protect people from natural hazards such as avalanches and floods.
wichtigste: The FOEN is the federal environment office and belongs to the department DETEC.
It is based in Ittigen near Bern and was created in 2006.
It deals with water, air, soil, forests, noise, waste and climate.
According to the FOEN's Red Lists, about a third of the species assessed in Switzerland are threatened (as of 2023).
About half of Switzerland's forest is protection forest.
Protection forest protects villages and roads from avalanches, rockfall and landslides.
The FOEN gives warnings about natural hazards such as floods.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office for the Environment** is the federal specialist office for all environmental questions. It was created in 2006, when the former Federal Office for the Environment, Forests and Landscape was merged with parts of the Federal Office for Water and Geology. The FOEN belongs to DETEC and is based in Ittigen near Bern. It prepares laws and helps the cantons to put them into practice.

**Biodiversity**, that is, the variety of animals, plants and fungi, is an important task of the FOEN. The **Red Lists** show which species are endangered in Switzerland. About a third of the species assessed are considered threatened, especially species in wetlands and waters. That is why the FOEN supports protected areas, moors and floodplains.

About a third of Switzerland's area is covered with forest. About half of it is **protection forest**. On steep slopes this forest stops avalanches, rockfall and landslides and so protects villages, roads and railway lines. The FOEN makes sure that such forests are looked after and stay healthy.

The FOEN measures how high the water is and how clean it is in many rivers and lakes. When **floods** threaten, it issues warnings so that municipalities can prepare. It also supports protective structures such as embankments and avalanche barriers. Much of this information can be found on the federal natural hazards platform.

The FOEN monitors air quality and noise, for example along motorways. It is also responsible for **climate policy**, that is, measures against the warming of the Earth. It also sets rules for waste and recycling. The fact that Switzerland collects a lot of glass, PET and paper is partly due to these rules.

begriffe.erklaerung: The variety of all living things and their habitats.
A list that shows which animal and plant species are threatened.
Forest that protects people and buildings from avalanches, falling rocks and landslides.
A natural event such as a flood or an avalanche that can cause damage.

gewusst: A healthy protection forest can give as much protection as expensive avalanche barriers made of steel and concrete.
The FOEN runs measuring stations that report the water levels of rivers and lakes round the clock.
Protecting the wolf, the lynx and the beaver is also one of the FOEN's topics.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Council is the government of Switzerland. It has seven members, who lead the country together and each head a department. Like Parliament, it sits in the Federal Palace in Bern.
wichtigste: The Federal Council is the government of Switzerland and has seven members.
It is the executive, that is, the power that carries things out at federal level.
The members are elected by the United Federal Assembly.
Each member heads one of the seven departments.
The President of the Confederation is elected afresh from the Federal Council every year.
Under the collegiality principle, the Federal Council decides together and presents its decisions with one voice.
The largest parties govern together; this is called concordance.

abschnitte.text: Since 1848 Switzerland has been a modern federal state with a **Federal Constitution**. Since then the Federal Council has existed as the government. It is the **executive**, which governs and puts laws into practice, while Parliament, as the legislature, makes the laws. The Federal Council and Parliament sit in the Federal Palace in Bern.

abschnitte.titel: How do you become a Federal Councillor?
abschnitte.text: The seven members are elected by the **United Federal Assembly**, that is, by the National Council and the Council of States together. The election takes place every four years after the National Council elections. Once elected, members are usually re-elected and often stay in office for eight to twelve years. If someone resigns, the Federal Assembly elects a successor.

In the Federal Council there is no boss; all members are equal. Under the **collegiality principle**, decisions are made together and presented to the outside world with one voice, even if a member had a different opinion. The largest parties sit together in the Federal Council instead of there being a strong opposition. This is called **concordance democracy**.

Every year the Federal Assembly elects one member of the Federal Council as President of the Confederation. This person stays in office for only one year and has no special powers. The President chairs the meetings of the Federal Council and represents Switzerland at important events. In 2026 Guy Parmelin is President of the Confederation.

Each member of the Federal Council heads a **department**, that is, a part of the federal administration. There is the Department of Foreign Affairs, the Department of Home Affairs, the Department of Justice, the Department of Defence, the Department of Finance, the Department of Economic Affairs and the Department of the Environment and Transport. Parliament can oblige the Federal Council to act with a motion. With a postulate, on the other hand, it only asks it to look into something.

begriffe.erklaerung: The government, which puts laws into practice and leads the country.
Parliament, which makes the laws.
The rule that the Federal Council decides together and speaks with one voice.
The large parties govern together and look for compromises.
A large area of the federal administration headed by a member of the Federal Council.

gewusst: From 1959 to 2003 the Federal Council always had the same party make-up; this was called the magic formula.
In 1984 Elisabeth Kopp was the first woman elected to the Federal Council.
Federal Councillors often move about Bern quite normally without bodyguards.

t2gpref.t: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI)

teile.einleitung: The State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation, SERI for short (in German SBFI), is the federal specialist office for education, science and new ideas. It looks after vocational apprenticeships, universities and cooperation with research programmes all over the world. In this way it helps Switzerland to be one of the most innovative countries.
wichtigste: SERI belongs to the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER).
It was created in 2013 from the State Secretariat for Education and Research and the Federal Office for Professional Education and Technology.
Together with the cantons and business, it is responsible for vocational education.
It supports universities and research, for example through the Swiss National Science Foundation and Innosuisse.
It represents Switzerland in international research organisations such as CERN and the European Space Agency ESA.
Compulsory schooling, on the other hand, is the responsibility of the cantons, not SERI.

abschnitte.text: SERI is a federal authority based in Bern. A **state secretariat** is an especially important federal office headed by a State Secretary. State Secretaries may also represent Switzerland abroad. SERI was created on 1 January 2013 to bring education, research and innovation together under one roof.

About two thirds of young people in Switzerland do a **vocational apprenticeship** after school. They work at the training company and attend vocational school at the same time; this is called the dual system. Together with the professional associations, SERI issues the training regulations for more than 200 apprenticeship trades. With the **vocational baccalaureate**, the way to a university of applied sciences is then also open.

Together with the cantons, SERI is responsible for **higher education institutions**, that is, universities, universities of applied sciences and universities of teacher education. It supports the cantonal universities with federal contributions. Together with the cantons, the federal government also recognises the academic baccalaureate. The two Federal Institutes of Technology in Zurich and Lausanne belong to the ETH Domain, which comes directly under the federal government.

The federal government supports research mainly through two organisations. The **Swiss National Science Foundation** supports basic research at universities. **Innosuisse** helps companies and researchers turn new ideas into products that can be sold. SERI prepares the laws and funding with which this support is paid for.

Research knows no borders, which is why Switzerland works closely with other countries. SERI represents Switzerland, for example, at **CERN** near Geneva and in the European Space Agency ESA. It also negotiates participation in the EU's big research programmes such as Horizon Europe. Through the Swissnex network, Switzerland is also present in important science cities around the world.

begriffe.erklaerung: Training in which you work in a company and go to school at the same time.
A new idea that becomes a useful product or process.
An especially important federal office whose head may represent Switzerland internationally.
Research that wants to understand how the world works, without immediately planning a product.

gewusst: For many years Switzerland has been in first place in the Global Innovation Index of the UN organisation WIPO.
In Switzerland you can make a career with an apprenticeship and further training just as well as with a university degree.

t5d2i31.t: Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS)

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport, DDPS for short (in German VBS), looks after Switzerland's security. This includes the army, protecting the population in disasters and also promoting sport. It is also responsible for cybersecurity and for surveying the country.
wichtigste: The DDPS is one of the seven federal departments.
Since 2025 it has been headed by Federal Councillor Martin Pfister.
The Swiss Armed Forces belong to the DDPS.
The Federal Office for Civil Protection prepares Switzerland for disasters and emergencies.
The Federal Office of Sport in Magglingen also belongs to the DDPS.
Since 2024 the Federal Office for Cybersecurity (NCSC) has been responsible for defending against cyber attacks.
Swisstopo, the Federal Office of Topography, makes the official national maps.

abschnitte.text: The **DDPS** is the department that looks after security and sport. Its abbreviation stands for Defence, Civil Protection and Sport. Since April 2025 Federal Councillor Martin Pfister has headed the department; before him it was Viola Amherd. Its headquarters is in the East Wing of the Federal Palace in Bern.

The **Swiss Armed Forces** are a militia army, which means that most of their members are not professional soldiers. Swiss men have a duty to do military service, and women can serve voluntarily. Anyone who does not want to do military service can, under certain conditions, do civilian service instead. The army protects the country but also helps in natural disasters and at large events.

The **Federal Office for Civil Protection** prepares Switzerland for emergencies such as floods, earthquakes or power cuts. It runs the warning system with sirens and the Alertswiss app. Every year on the first Wednesday in February, the sirens are tested all over Switzerland. **Civil defence** is also part of civil protection.

Since 2024 there has been the **Federal Office for Cybersecurity**, NCSC for short. It helps authorities, companies and private individuals to protect themselves against attacks from the internet. There you can, for example, report attempts at fraud by e-mail. The Federal Intelligence Service also belongs to the DDPS; it is meant to spot dangers such as terrorism or espionage early.

The **Federal Office of Sport**, based in Magglingen, also belongs to the DDPS; it looks after Youth+Sport, for example. Another office is **swisstopo**, the Federal Office of Topography. It surveys Switzerland and publishes the well-known national maps. With the swisstopo app, hikers can plan their routes.

begriffe.erklaerung: An army in which most soldiers serve alongside their normal jobs.
An organisation that helps in disasters and protects the population.
Protecting computers and networks from attacks and misuse.
The precise description of the landscape with its mountains, valleys and waters.

gewusst: During the yearly siren test in February, about 5000 sirens wail at the same time all over Switzerland.
Switzerland's national maps are regarded worldwide as especially accurate and beautifully designed.
The fact that sport and the army are in the same department goes back to the former physical training for young men.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Culture, FOC for short (in German BAK), is the culture office of the Swiss Confederation. It supports art, film, music, literature and design and protects valuable buildings and cultural property. In this way it helps to keep Switzerland's varied culture alive.
wichtigste: The FOC belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and is based in Bern.
It supports film-making and culture throughout Switzerland.
It deals with the care of historic monuments, heritage protection and archaeology.
The Swiss National Library in Bern belongs to the FOC.
It awards Swiss prizes for art, design, film, literature, music and theatre.
It supports the national languages, especially Romansh and Italian.
The federal government sets the goals of its cultural policy for four years at a time in the culture message.

abschnitte.text: The FOC is a federal office in the **Department of Home Affairs**. In Switzerland, culture is mainly the responsibility of the cantons and municipalities. The federal government takes on tasks that are important for the whole country. How the federal government supports culture is set out every four years in the **culture message**, which Parliament decides on. The FOC carries out these plans and works closely with the Pro Helvetia foundation.

A large part of the money goes to **film-making**. The FOC supports Swiss feature films, documentaries and animated films so that they can be made at all. Every year the Swiss Film Award is presented. There are also Swiss prizes for art, design, literature, music, theatre and dance. In this way artists become better known and can make a living from their work.

The FOC helps to preserve old castles, churches, bridges and townscapes. For this it pays contributions to the **care of historic monuments** and to archaeological excavations. It keeps the federal inventory of townscapes worth protecting, ISOS for short. It also makes sure that no stolen or looted **cultural property** is brought into Switzerland or sold here. World Heritage Sites such as the Old City of Bern or the Abbey of St Gallen are also close to its heart.

The **Swiss National Library** in Bern belongs to the FOC. It collects everything published in Switzerland or about Switzerland, that is, books, newspapers, posters and much more. The FOC also looks after some museums, for example the Museum of Musical Automatons in Seewen in the canton of Solothurn and the Museo Vela in Ticino. It also manages the federal art collection with many thousands of works. Many of them hang on loan in museums and embassies.

Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. The FOC supports **multilingualism** and exchange between the language regions. Romansh in the Grisons and Italian in Ticino and the southern Grisons receive special support. The culture of the Yenish and Sinti, who live as Travellers, is also supported. The FOC also promotes reading and the musical education of children and young people.

begriffe.erklaerung: A federal plan that sets out for four years how culture will be supported.
The work of preserving old and valuable buildings.
