An object or building that is important for history and culture.
When several languages are spoken in a country or by one person.

gewusst: The National Library has to collect not only books but also archive Swiss websites.
The Museum of Musical Automatons in Seewen has music boxes and organs that make music without any musicians.
In Switzerland the cantons, towns and municipalities together spend much more money on culture than the federal government.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Social Insurance Office, FSIO for short (in German BSV), looks after social security in Switzerland. It is responsible for the AVS, disability insurance and many other insurance schemes that protect people in old age, illness or accident. Family and youth policy is also one of its tasks.
wichtigste: The FSIO belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and is based in Bern.
The AVS was introduced in 1948 and is financed mainly on a pay-as-you-go basis.
Since 1972 the three-pillar principle of pension provision has been set out in the Federal Constitution.
The AVS contribution rate is 8.7 per cent of the wage, paid half each by employer and employee (as of 2026).
In occupational pension provision a minimum conversion rate of 6.8 per cent applies (as of 2026).
Pillar 3a belongs to the third pillar, private pension provision.
The FSIO runs the national platform Youth and Media to promote media skills.

abschnitte.text: The FSIO is the federal specialist office for **social insurance**. It belongs to the Department of Home Affairs and prepares laws, for example reforms of the AVS. It also checks that the insurance schemes work properly. However, pensions are not paid out by the FSIO itself but by the **compensation offices** and the disability insurance offices. Besides pension provision, the FSIO looks after families, children and young people.

Old-age and survivors' insurance, **AVS** for short, was introduced in 1948. It pays pensions to older people and to widows, widowers and orphans. It is financed mainly on a **pay-as-you-go basis**: today's workers' contributions directly pay today's pensions. The contribution is 8.7 per cent of gross pay, that is, pay before any deductions, and the employer pays half of it. The normal retirement age is 65; for women it is being raised step by step from 64 to 65.

Since 1972 the **three-pillar principle** has been in the Federal Constitution. The first pillar is the AVS together with disability insurance; it is meant to cover basic needs. The second pillar is **occupational pension provision** with the pension funds, into which employees and employers pay together. On retirement, the savings are converted into a pension using the conversion rate, at least 6.8 per cent in the compulsory part. The third pillar is private pension provision, for example tax-favoured saving in pillar 3a.

**Disability insurance** (IV) has existed since 1960. It helps people who can no longer work, or can only work part of the time, because of an illness or an accident. The income compensation scheme replaces part of the wage, for example during military service or maternity. Supplementary benefits help when the pension is not enough to live on. Compulsory health insurance is now looked after by the Federal Office of Public Health; the lowest standard deductible for adults is 300 francs (as of 2026).

The FSIO is also responsible for **family allowances**, that is, money that parents receive for their children. It supports work with children and young people and is committed to protecting children. With the **Youth and Media** platform, it helps children, young people, parents and teachers to use mobile phones, the internet and games safely and wisely. There are tips on topics such as screen time, cyberbullying and data protection. In this way the FSIO combines social security with support in everyday life.

begriffe.erklaerung: State insurance that helps people in old age, illness, accident or unemployment.
Today's workers' contributions directly pay today's pensions.
Pay before deductions such as AVS contributions are taken off.
The amount you pay yourself each year before the health insurance fund pays.
The percentage used to convert pension fund savings into a yearly pension.

gewusst: Everyone who lives or works in Switzerland gets their own AVS number, which begins with 756.
In 2024 the Swiss people voted for a 13th AVS pension payment, which will be paid once a year in addition from 2026.
Even students without an income have to pay AVS contributions from the age of 21.

tah5m1a.t: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security, FOCBS for short (in German BAZG), checks which goods and people come into and leave Switzerland. It collects charges, fights smuggling and ensures security at the border. Until 2021 it was called the Federal Customs Administration.
wichtigste: The FOCBS belongs to the Federal Department of Finance (FDF).
It has had its present name since 1 January 2022; before that it was called the Federal Customs Administration.
Since 1848 the federal government, and no longer the cantons, has been responsible for customs.
It checks goods, vehicles and people at the border and inside the country.
It collects charges such as value added tax on imports, the mineral oil tax and the heavy vehicle charge.
Sniffer dogs help to find drugs, cash or smuggled goods.
Because of the customs treaty of 1923, the FOCBS also checks the border between Liechtenstein and Austria.

abschnitte.text: The FOCBS is Switzerland's **customs authority**, with its headquarters in Bern. It has several thousand employees, who work at border crossings, airports and inside the country. In the past, customs and the Border Guard were separate areas; today they work closely together in the FOCBS. With the DaziT programme, customs is being largely digitised.

Until 1848 the cantons charged their own customs duties, even on bridges and roads inside Switzerland. When the federal state was founded, **customs** passed to the federal government. This made Switzerland a single economic area. For a long time customs duties were even the federal government's most important source of income.

A **customs duty** is a charge on goods brought across the border. Since 1 January 2024 Switzerland has abolished customs duties on industrial goods, but there are still duties on many foods. The FOCBS also collects value added tax on imported goods, the mineral oil tax on fuel, the tobacco tax and the performance-related heavy vehicle charge for lorries. In this way it takes in many billions of francs a year for the federal government.

During checks, the FOCBS looks for **smuggling**, for example of drugs, weapons, fake branded goods or protected animal species. Specially trained **sniffer dogs** help with this. They can pick out the tiniest traces of certain substances from a complex mixture of smells. The FOCBS also checks people, for example when looking for wanted criminals.

Switzerland is a country with a lot of **foreign trade**. By value, it exports mostly chemical and pharmaceutical products, followed by machines, watches and precision instruments (as of 2025). The FOCBS records all imports and exports and so supplies the foreign trade statistics. The rules for world trade go back to the GATT of 1947, from which the World Trade Organization WTO later developed.

When you come back from holiday, you may bring in goods worth up to 150 francs per person without value added tax (as of 2025). For meat, alcohol and tobacco there are also fixed **duty-free allowances**. Anyone carrying more can easily declare and pay for the goods with the QuickZoll app. Anyone who hides goods risks a fine.

begriffe.erklaerung: A charge on goods brought across the national border.
Secretly bringing goods into or out of a country to avoid charges or bans.
The amount of a product you may bring in without paying charges.
A charge for lorries calculated by weight and kilometres driven.

gewusst: Switzerland's national border is about 1900 kilometres long.
Liechtenstein and Switzerland have formed a single customs area since 1924, which is why there are no customs checks between the two countries.

teile.einleitung: The Price Supervisor is a federal office that makes sure prices in Switzerland are not abusively high. It is headed by the Price Supervisor, whom everyone simply calls “Monsieur Prix”. The office looks especially closely where there is hardly any competition.
wichtigste: The Price Supervisor protects consumers from abusively high prices.
The Price Supervisor is elected by the Federal Council and belongs to the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research.
The basis is the Price Supervision Act of 1986, after the people approved a popular initiative in 1982.
The office mainly checks prices of companies without real competition and charges made by authorities.
Examples are medicines, hospital tariffs, postal services, public transport, electricity and water charges.
Anyone can report prices that seem too high to them to the Price Supervisor.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland is regarded as a **high-price island**, because many things cost more here than in neighbouring countries. Normally competition makes sure that prices do not get too high. But when only one company offers something, this pressure is missing. Then **price supervision** steps in and checks whether the price is justified.

In the 1970s prices rose sharply, and the federal government temporarily introduced price supervision. In 1982 the people and the cantons approved a **popular initiative** by consumer organisations that called for permanent price supervision. The Price Supervision Act came into force in 1986. Since then the Price Supervisor has been a permanent institution.

abschnitte.titel: How does the Price Supervisor work?
abschnitte.text: The Price Supervisor examines the prices of companies that have a **dominant position in the market**. Often an agreement on a price cut is reached with the company; this is called an amicable settlement. If that does not work, the Price Supervisor can also order a cut. For prices set by authorities, for example charges for rubbish or water, the office may only make recommendations.

It is often about **medicines**, which are much more expensive in Switzerland than abroad. The tariffs of hospitals and doctors are also checked. Other topics are prices for postal services, trains and buses, charges for electricity and gas, or parking charges. The Price Supervisor often publishes price comparisons so that everyone can see where things are cheaper.

Anyone can send the Price Supervisor a **report** via the website if a price seems too high to them. Many thousands of such reports come in every year. They help the Price Supervisor see where problems exist. A well-known holder of the office was Stefan Meierhans, who held it from 2008 and often appeared in the media.

begriffe.erklaerung: A country where many goods cost much more than in neighbouring countries.
When several companies offer the same thing and compete for customers.
When only one company offers a product or a service.
An amount you pay an authority for a particular service.

gewusst: The nickname “Monsieur Prix” is French and means “Mister Price”.
The Price Supervisor is not a court but can achieve a great deal through publicity and negotiation.

tc2yd1j.t: Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC)

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications, DETEC for short (in German UVEK), is one of the seven federal departments. It is responsible for things that are part of our everyday lives, from the train to school to the electricity from the plug socket and mobile phone reception. At the same time it is meant to protect nature and the climate.
wichtigste: DETEC is one of the seven departments of the federal administration.
It is responsible for the environment, transport, energy and communications.
Since 2023 it has been headed by Federal Councillor Albert Rösti.
DETEC includes offices such as FEDRO, the FOT, FOCA, the SFOE, OFCOM and the FOEN.
It carries out the Energy Strategy 2050, which the people approved in 2017.
Through DETEC, the federal government owns companies such as SBB and Swiss Post.
Spatial planning is also one of its tasks.

abschnitte.text: **DETEC** is a department with an especially large number of different tasks. Its name lists its four main areas: the environment, transport, energy and communications. Since 2023 Federal Councillor Albert Rösti has headed the department. Its General Secretariat is in Bern.

For transport, DETEC has three federal offices. The **Federal Roads Office** looks after the motorways, the Federal Office of Transport looks after rail, buses and boats, and the Federal Office of Civil Aviation looks after air traffic. Large projects such as the NRLA with the Gotthard Base Tunnel were built under DETEC's supervision. The aim is a transport system that works well and puts as little strain as possible on the environment.

The **Swiss Federal Office of Energy** makes sure that Switzerland has enough electricity and heat. Important here is the **Energy Strategy 2050**, which the people approved in 2017. It provides that no new nuclear power stations will be built and that more renewable energy will be used. This includes hydropower, solar energy, wind and wood.

The **Federal Office for the Environment** protects water, air, forests, animals and plants and deals with the climate. The Federal Office for Spatial Development plans how settlements, agriculture and nature can all find room side by side. For example, it makes sure that not too much land is built on. A supervisory authority for the safety of nuclear power stations also belongs to DETEC's sphere.

The **Federal Office of Communications**, OFCOM for short, is responsible for radio, television, postal services and telecommunications. It allocates frequencies for mobile phones and makes sure that the basic supply of telephone and internet works. DETEC also represents the federal government as owner of SBB and Swiss Post. The federal government holds the majority of the shares in Swisscom.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large area of the federal administration headed by a member of the Federal Council.
Energy from sources that do not get used up, for example sun, wind and water.
Planning where building is allowed and where nature and agriculture have room.
A particular radio band over which mobile phones, for example, send and receive.

gewusst: DETEC is responsible for things as different as motorways, wolves and mobile phone masts.
Hydropower supplies most of the electricity in Switzerland.
Moritz Leuenberger headed DETEC for an especially long time, from 1995 to 2010.

teile.einleitung: SBB, the Swiss Federal Railways, is the largest railway company in Switzerland. Its red and white trains connect towns and villages all over the country. The Swiss travel by train more than almost any other people in Europe.
wichtigste: SBB was founded in 1902 and belongs to the federal government.
On 20 February 1898 the people voted for the federal government to buy back the large private railways.
The first entirely Swiss railway was the Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn from Zurich to Baden in 1847.
The Gotthard Base Tunnel has been in operation since 2016 and, at about 57 kilometres, is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
SBB runs on standard gauge, that is, with about 1435 millimetres between the rails.
SBB's headquarters is in Bern.

abschnitte.text: The first railway line entirely on Swiss soil opened in 1847 and ran from Zurich to Baden. It was called the **Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn**, after a pastry from Baden that could now be taken fresh to Zurich quickly. The opening train was pulled by the locomotive Limmat. The gauge was the **standard gauge** of about 1435 millimetres, which comes from early English railways and is the most common in the world today.

At first, private companies built the railways, and they often competed with each other. On 20 February 1898 the people decided that the federal government should buy back the large private railways. From this, the **Swiss Federal Railways** was formed in 1902. Since 1999 SBB has been a special public limited company that belongs entirely to the federal government.

Because Switzerland has no coal but plenty of hydropower, it began to **electrify** its railways early. From 1922 the Gotthard railway could be run electrically all the way. Today practically all SBB trains run on electricity. SBB produces a large part of the electricity in its own hydropower stations.

In 1882 the Gotthard railway opened with a summit tunnel about 15 kilometres long. Much deeper under the mountain lies the **Gotthard Base Tunnel**, which opened in 2016 and is about 57 kilometres long. It is the longest railway tunnel in the world. Together with the Ceneri Base Tunnel, which opened in 2020, it forms a flat railway through the Alps, the NRLA.

SBB runs to a **clock-face timetable**, which means that many trains leave every hour or half hour at the same minute. With the GA travelcard you can travel by train almost anywhere in Switzerland for a year. The station clock with its red second hand, designed by Hans Hilfiker, is famous. As well as people, the subsidiary SBB Cargo also carries goods.

begriffe.erklaerung: The most common distance between the rails, about 1435 millimetres.
A tunnel deep down through the foot of a mountain range so that the line stays flat.
A timetable in which trains run at regular intervals at the same minute.
A yearly ticket for almost all trains, buses and boats in Switzerland.

gewusst: The SBB station clock stops briefly at every full minute until a signal lets it carry on.
The Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn took about 45 minutes for the journey from Zurich to Baden.

teile.einleitung: Swiss Post delivers letters and parcels to every corner of Switzerland, from the town centre to the remote mountain village. It belongs to the federal government and is one of the best-known companies in the country. The yellow PostBuses and the bank PostFinance also belong to Swiss Post.
wichtigste: Swiss Post is a company that belongs entirely to the federal government.
With the federal state of 1848, postal services, coins, and weights and measures were standardised throughout Switzerland.
The postman or postwoman brings letters and parcels right to the door.
PostBus and the bank PostFinance belong to Swiss Post.
Swiss Post must provide a universal service throughout Switzerland.
Many people vote by post and send their voting envelope by post.

abschnitte.text: In the past, the cantons and private companies had their own postal services with different prices. With the **federal state** of 1848, postal services, coins, and weights and measures were standardised, and from 1849 there was a federal post. Later, post, telephone and telegraph were combined into the **PTT**. In 1998 the PTT was split into Swiss Post and the telecommunications company Swisscom.

Every day Swiss Post delivers millions of letters, newspapers and parcels. Since 1964 every place in Switzerland has had a four-digit **postcode** so that items can be sorted quickly. You can send letters by A-Post, which usually arrives the next working day, or by cheaper B-Post. Because many people write e-mails today, there are fewer letters but many more parcels from online shopping.

The yellow **PostBuses** have been running for over a hundred years and serve especially villages in the mountains. They drive over Alpine passes such as the Gotthard, the Furka or the Grimsel. Their three-tone horn is well known; its tune comes from the overture to Rossini's opera William Tell. In the past, PostBuses also brought the post to the villages; today they are mainly buses for travellers.

The bank **PostFinance**, where many people have an account and pay bills, belongs to Swiss Post. Swiss Post has a legal mission, the **universal service**. This means it must carry letters and parcels throughout Switzerland on the same terms, even to remote places. Because many post offices have few customers, some have been closed and replaced by branches in shops.

Swiss Post also plays an important role in votes. Votes usually take place on a Sunday, but many people vote by post beforehand. Along with the papers comes the **polling card**, a document showing that you are entitled to vote. You put the completed ballot paper together with the card in the voting envelope and send it by post to the municipality.

begriffe.erklaerung: The person who delivers letters and parcels; in Switzerland called “Pöstler”.
A four-digit number that shows which place a letter is going to.
The duty to provide important services to everyone throughout the country.
An envelope in which you send your ballot paper by post.

gewusst: In 1964 Switzerland was one of the first countries in the world to introduce postcodes for the whole country.
As early as 1843 the canton of Zurich issued its own stamps, the Zurich 4 and Zurich 6, which are now among the most valuable stamps in the world.

teile.einleitung: The ambulance service helps people who suddenly fall ill or are seriously injured. It comes with an ambulance and treats patients right where they are. In Switzerland you can reach it on the emergency number 144.
wichtigste: In Switzerland you call the ambulance service on 144.
You can reach the fire brigade on 118 and Rega on 1414.
The European emergency number 112 also works in Switzerland.
Specially trained paramedics work in the ambulance.
In serious emergencies an emergency doctor comes as well.
With blue lights and a siren, the ambulance is allowed to get through faster.
Children and young people with worries can get help on 147.

abschnitte.text: The ambulance service brings medical help to where it is needed. It treats people after accidents, during a heart attack, when they cannot breathe properly or after poisoning. Then it takes them safely to **hospital**. Because every minute often counts, treatment begins at the scene and during the journey.

Usually two people travel in an ambulance. The **paramedics** have completed three years of training at a college of higher education. In life-threatening emergencies an **emergency doctor** comes too, sometimes in their own car or by helicopter. For missions in the mountains or over long distances, Rega helps from the air.

abschnitte.titel: From the emergency call to the mission
abschnitte.text: If you dial 144, you get through to an **ambulance control centre**. There, experts ask exactly what has happened and send out the nearest suitable vehicle. On the phone they also give instructions, for example how to do chest compressions until help arrives. In Switzerland the aim is for the ambulance service to be on the scene within 15 minutes in most cases.

With **blue lights** and a siren, the ambulance shows that it is on an urgent journey. Other vehicles must then make room and pull over. The siren sounds higher when the vehicle is coming towards you and lower when it is moving away. This is called the **Doppler effect**; it happens because the sound waves in front of the vehicle are squeezed together.

Until the ambulance arrives, anyone can give **first aid**. First check that it is safe for you, then call 144. An unconscious person who is breathing normally is placed in the recovery position. If they are not breathing, chest compressions are needed at once and, if possible, a defibrillator, which hangs in many stations and sports halls.

begriffe.erklaerung: The vehicle that takes sick and injured people to hospital; in Switzerland often called “Ambulanz”.
A professional who treats and transports sick and injured people in an emergency.
A doctor who comes straight to the scene in serious emergencies.
A device that can use an electric shock to bring a heart that has stopped back into the right rhythm.
A sound is higher when its source comes closer and lower when it moves away.

gewusst: The lettering on the bonnet of many ambulances is written back to front so that drivers can read it correctly in their rear-view mirror.
The star with the snake on many rescue vehicles is called the Star of Life and is a worldwide symbol of rescue services.
Experts in the control centre can guide callers step by step through resuscitation over the phone.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Tax Administration, FTA for short (in German ESTV), is the federal authority for taxes. It makes sure that the federal government collects its taxes, which pay for things such as railways, the army and education. The best-known tax it collects is value added tax.
wichtigste: The FTA is the federal tax authority and belongs to the Federal Department of Finance.
It is based in Bern.
It is responsible for value added tax, withholding tax, stamp duties and direct federal tax.
Value added tax is included in the price of many goods and services.
Since 2024 the standard rate of value added tax has been 8.1 per cent.
Children pay taxes too, for example value added tax when shopping.
Value added tax is the federal government's largest source of income.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Tax Administration** is a federal office in the Federal Department of Finance. It is based in Bern and employs more than a thousand people. Its task is to collect federal taxes. It also prepares new tax laws and advises the Federal Council.

**Value added tax**, VAT for short, is a tax charged on most goods and services. It is already included in the sale price, so you often do not even notice it. Since 2024 the standard rate has been 8.1 per cent; a reduced rate of 2.6 per cent applies to food, books and medicines. Because it is charged on every purchase, children pay taxes too, for example when they buy an ice cream.

**Withholding tax** of 35 per cent is deducted, for example, from interest and dividends. Anyone who declares this income correctly in their tax return gets the money back. **Stamp duties** are charged, for example, when trading securities. Direct federal tax on income is collected by the cantons and passed on to the federal government; the FTA supervises this.

Value added tax was introduced in Switzerland in 1995. It replaced the older **turnover tax on goods**, WUST for short. Because the federal government may only collect taxes if the constitution allows it, the people and the cantons must vote on important tax changes. This is how the increase to 8.1 per cent in 2024 was decided, to strengthen the AVS.

In Switzerland not only the federal government but also the cantons and municipalities collect taxes. That is why most people fill in a **tax return** for their canton once a year. Tax rates differ from canton to canton, which is called **tax competition**. The FTA works closely with the cantonal tax administrations and also exchanges information with other countries.

begriffe.erklaerung: Money that everyone must pay to the state so that it can carry out its tasks.
A tax that is included in the price of most goods and services.
A tax on interest and dividends that you get back if you declare them correctly.
A form in which you state your income and assets for the tax authority.

gewusst: Value added tax in Switzerland is much lower than in most European countries, where it is often around 20 per cent.
A special rate of 3.8 per cent applies to overnight stays in hotels.
On every till receipt you can see how much value added tax is included in the price.

teile.einleitung: Swisscom is the largest telecommunications company in Switzerland. It offers mobile phone contracts, internet, landline telephone and television. The federal government owns the majority of the shares; the remaining shares can be bought on the stock exchange.
wichtigste: Swisscom is the largest provider of telephone, mobile phone and internet services in Switzerland.
Swisscom grew out of the former PTT, which combined post, telephone and telegraph.
Since 1998 Swisscom has been a public limited company listed on the stock exchange.
The federal government holds the majority of the shares.
Its headquarters is in Ittigen near Bern.
In Italy, Swisscom owns the telecommunications company Fastweb.

abschnitte.text: In the past, post and telephone in Switzerland were a single state company, the **PTT**. In 1998 the PTT was split up, and the telephone part became Swisscom. In the same year its shares were listed on the **stock exchange**. At the same time the telephone market was opened up, so that other companies such as Sunrise and Salt could offer services too.

Swisscom runs one of Switzerland's mobile networks, with thousands of masts. With it you can make calls and surf the internet almost everywhere, even in many mountain valleys. Through fibre-optic cables, Swisscom brings fast internet to homes and businesses. The new **5G network** allows even faster data transmission.

With its blue service, Swisscom shows television, films and sport. The company also runs data centres and helps businesses with information technology. In the past there were yellow and later green **phone boxes** everywhere, which you used with coins or cards. Because almost everyone has a mobile phone, most public phone boxes have been removed.

By law, the federal government must own the majority of Swisscom's shares. On behalf of the federal government, Swisscom provides the **universal service**, that is, telephone and internet for everyone in Switzerland. Swisscom's profits bring the federal government money every year. In politics there are repeated debates about whether the federal government should sell shares.

In 2007 Swisscom bought the Italian company **Fastweb**. Later Swisscom also took over Vodafone Italia and merged it with Fastweb. This makes Swisscom a large provider in Italy as well. In Switzerland, however, Swisscom remains the best-known brand for communications.

begriffe.erklaerung: Transmitting speech, pictures and data over long distances.
A thin cable made of glass that transmits data very fast using light.
A network of masts through which mobile phones make calls and surf.
A portion of a company that you can buy and sell.

gewusst: In Switzerland a mobile phone is also called a “Natel”, a name that comes from the former PTT.
Public phone boxes have almost completely disappeared in Switzerland; some have been turned into book cabinets.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Sport, FOSPO for short (in German BASPO), is the federal body that looks after sport and exercise in Switzerland. Its headquarters is in Magglingen, high above Lake Biel. Perhaps you have taken part in a Youth+Sport camp yourself, which FOSPO supports.
wichtigste: FOSPO is Switzerland's Federal Office of Sport.
Its headquarters is in Magglingen above Biel in the canton of Bern.
It belongs to the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
Its most important support programme is called Youth+Sport and is meant for children and young people aged 5 to 20.
The Swiss Federal Institute of Sport Magglingen belongs to FOSPO.
In Tenero in Ticino, FOSPO runs a large sports centre for young people.
FOSPO also works for fair, clean sport without doping.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Sport** is a section of the federal administration. It belongs to the DDPS, which is also home to the army and civil protection. Its task is to promote sport and exercise for everyone in Switzerland. This includes grassroots sport for everyone as well as top-level sport.

The headquarters is in **Magglingen**, a place on a sunny terrace above Biel and Lake Biel. There are sports halls, grass pitches, an athletics ground and accommodation for training camps. The Federal Gymnastics and Sports School was founded here as early as 1944. A second important site is the youth sports centre in **Tenero** on Lake Maggiore, where school classes and clubs can hold camps.

**Youth+Sport**, J+S for short, is the federal government's largest sports support programme. It is aimed at children and young people aged 5 to 20. Clubs and schools receive federal money if they offer courses and camps with trained leaders. J+S has existed since 1972, and today hundreds of thousands of children take part every year in many sports, from football to mountaineering.

The **Swiss Federal Institute of Sport Magglingen**, SFISM for short, belongs to FOSPO. There you can, for example, study sports science or train as a coach. Researchers study how to train better and how exercise strengthens health. Leaders for J+S are also trained according to FOSPO's guidelines.

Together with the umbrella organisation Swiss Olympic, FOSPO supports Swiss top-level sport. For athletes in the army there are even special elite sport recruit schools. The office also works for **fair play** and against doping. The doping tests themselves are carried out by the independent foundation Swiss Sport Integrity.

begriffe.erklaerung: A specialist office of the federal administration that deals with a particular subject.
A federal programme that supports sports courses and camps for 5- to 20-year-olds.
Sport that many people do in their free time, not just professionals.
Banned substances or methods used to boost your own performance artificially.

gewusst: In French Magglingen is called Macolin, and FOSPO is known there in both languages.
Many Swiss Olympic athletes have trained in Magglingen.
Anyone who wants to lead a J+S camp needs special training for it.

teile.einleitung: RUAG is a technology company that belongs to the federal government and works mainly for the Swiss Armed Forces. It maintains and repairs aircraft, helicopters, vehicles and other military equipment. The company was formed in 1999 from the federal government's former armaments works.
wichtigste: RUAG is a company owned by the federal government.
The company was formed in 1999 from the federal armaments works.
Its most important task is to maintain the Swiss Armed Forces' equipment and keep it ready for use.
The name originally comes from the German for armaments company limited.
Its headquarters is in Bern.
The space division was separated off and is now called Beyond Gravity.

abschnitte.text: **RUAG** is a public limited company whose shares belong to the federal government. It is an important partner of the **Swiss Armed Forces**. A company that makes or looks after weapons and military equipment is called a defence company. With RUAG, the federal government wants to make sure that the army can repair its equipment itself within the country, even in a crisis.

In the past the federal government made weapons, ammunition and aircraft parts in its own workshops, for example in Thun, Emmen and Altdorf. In 1999 these **armaments works** were combined into one company, which was called RUAG. Later RUAG grew and also bought companies abroad. From 2020 the company was reorganised and split into a part for the army and an international part.

RUAG looks after the air force's fighter jets, for example the F/A-18. The experts inspect the aircraft, replace parts and modernise the technology. Helicopters, tanks and radio equipment are also maintained. This work is called **maintenance**, and it makes sure everything works safely.

RUAG's former space division built, for example, fairings for rockets such as the European Ariane. Since 2022 this part has been called **Beyond Gravity**. The ammunition division Ammotec was sold. The federal government wants RUAG to concentrate on its tasks for the Swiss Armed Forces.

Because RUAG belongs to the state, the company is often debated in politics. Questions include, for example, what business a federal company may do. The export of war material is also strictly regulated in Switzerland. Parliament and the Federal Council set the **strategic goals** for the company.

begriffe.erklaerung: A company that makes or looks after weapons or military equipment.
Checking, looking after and repairing machines so that they work safely.
A form of company whose owners hold portions called shares.
A company that belongs entirely or mostly to the federal government.

gewusst: Parts built at RUAG for rockets have already flown into space.
The workshops in Emmen near Lucerne are right next to a military airfield.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Statistical Office, FSO for short (in German BFS), collects figures about Switzerland and its population. It knows, for example, how many people live here, how many children are born and how fast prices are rising. It is based in Neuchâtel.
wichtigste: The FSO is the federal government's central statistics office and is based in Neuchâtel.
It belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA).
At the end of 2024, about a quarter of the permanent resident population did not have a Swiss passport.
In 2024 the birth rate was about 1.3 children per woman.
The FSO calculates the Swiss consumer price index, which measures inflation.
For statistics, the FSO divides Switzerland into 7 major regions.
Its figures help politics, business and schools to make good decisions.

abschnitte.text: The FSO collects, checks and publishes **statistics** on almost every area of life. These include population, work, health, education, transport, the environment and elections. The figures often come from the registers of municipalities and cantons or from surveys. Anyone can look at the results free of charge on the internet.

Federal statistics began in 1860 with the Federal Statistical Bureau in Bern. Since 1998 the federal office has been housed in **Neuchâtel**, in a modern building near the station. In the past, a large **census** was held every ten years, in which every household filled in a questionnaire. Since 2010 the FSO has instead mainly used registers and yearly sample surveys.

At the end of 2024, about 9 million people lived in Switzerland. About a quarter of them did not have a Swiss passport. In 2024 the **birth rate** was about 1.3 children per woman, which is very low compared with the past. The most common cause of death is heart and circulatory disease, as the statistics for 2022 show.

Every month the FSO calculates the **Swiss consumer price index**, CPI for short. To do this, it follows how the prices of a typical basket of goods, including bread, rents, clothes and much more, change. The FSO also shows that over 99 per cent of Swiss companies are SMEs with fewer than 250 employees, namely about 99.7 per cent in 2021. The quarterly estimates of gross domestic product, however, are published by SECO.

The FSO also analyses elections and votes. In the 2023 National Council elections, **turnout** was about 47 per cent. So that areas can be compared, the FSO divides Switzerland into 7 major regions, such as the Lake Geneva region, Espace Mittelland or Ticino. In this way you can compare, for example, where more people travel to work by train.

begriffe.erklaerung: Collecting and analysing lots of figures in order to see something general.
When goods and services become more expensive on average.
The average number of children a woman has during her life.
A selection of people who are surveyed instead of asking everyone.

gewusst: The FSO does not survey everyone; for the structural survey it asks only a sample of about 200,000 people each year.
From the FSO's figures we even know which first names are most popular for babies in Switzerland.
A turnout of about 47 per cent means that fewer than half of those entitled to vote actually voted.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Transport, FOT for short (in German BAV), is the federal specialist office for public transport. It looks after trains, buses, trams, boats and cable cars. Thanks to its work, people in Switzerland can get almost anywhere by public transport.
wichtigste: The FOT is the Federal Office of Transport and belongs to the department DETEC.
It is based in Ittigen near Bern.
It is responsible for rail, buses, trams, boats and cable cars.
The FOT plans the expansion of the rail network and distributes federal money for it.
It monitors safety in public transport.
At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
Switzerland is one of the countries where people travel by train the most.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Transport** belongs to the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications. It is based in Ittigen near Bern. It is responsible for **public transport**, that is, means of transport that everyone can use. These include railways, PostBuses, trams, boats on the lakes and cable cars in the mountains.

Together with the railway companies, the FOT plans how the network will be expanded in the future. Since 2016 the money for this has come from the **Railway Infrastructure Fund**, which voters approved in 2014. It pays for new tracks, stations and tunnels and for maintaining existing facilities. The aim is for more trains to run and for connections to fit together well.

A major project was the **New Railway Link through the Alps**, NRLA for short. It includes the Lötschberg Base Tunnel from 2007, the Gotthard Base Tunnel from 2016 and the Ceneri Base Tunnel from 2020. At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. The NRLA is meant above all to help carry goods through the Alps by rail instead of by lorry.

The FOT is also a **supervisory authority**. It checks that railways, buses and cable cars are built and run safely. New vehicles and installations need a permit from the FOT before they may carry passengers. After an accident, the office can demand improvements.

Many bus routes and regional trains in the countryside would not pay for themselves. That is why the federal government and the cantons together pay part of the costs, so that even small villages stay connected. The FOT orders such services in **regional transport** together with the cantons. In this way, for example, the PostBus also runs into remote mountain valleys.

begriffe.erklaerung: Means of transport such as trains, buses and trams that anyone may use with a ticket.
New Railway Link through the Alps, a building project with long railway tunnels through the Alps.
A body that checks whether rules are being followed.
A pot of money intended for a particular purpose.

gewusst: Work on building the Gotthard Base Tunnel went on for about 17 years.
Chairlifts and gondola lifts in ski resorts also need a federal permit.
A large part of the freight traffic through the Swiss Alps goes by rail instead of by road.

tpr4v7q.t: Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER)

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research, EAER for short (in German WBF), deals with work, the economy, agriculture, education and research. It makes sure that the Swiss economy works well and that young people get a good education. Vocational education and the two Federal Institutes of Technology belong to it.
wichtigste: The EAER is one of the seven federal departments.
Since 2021 it has been headed by Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin.
The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) belongs to the EAER.
The State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI) is responsible for vocational education and universities.
Agriculture also belongs to the EAER, with the Federal Office for Agriculture.
ETH Zurich and EPFL in Lausanne belong to the ETH Domain, which is assigned to the EAER.
Until 2012 the department was called the Federal Department of Economic Affairs.

abschnitte.text: The **EAER** is the department for economic affairs, education and research. Until the end of 2012 it was called the Department of Economic Affairs; then education and research were added. Since 2021 Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin has headed the department. Its General Secretariat is in the East Wing of the Federal Palace in Bern.

**SECO**, the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, is the EAER's most important office for the economy. It negotiates trade agreements with other countries and watches the state of the economy. It publishes, for example, the unemployment figures and the quarterly estimates of gross domestic product. It also looks after unemployment insurance and the protection of employees.

**SERI** is responsible for vocational education, universities and research. In Switzerland about two thirds of young people do a **vocational apprenticeship** after compulsory school. The ETH Domain includes ETH Zurich and EPFL in Lausanne, which are among the best universities in the world. The funding agency Innosuisse supports companies that develop new ideas.

The **Federal Office for Agriculture** looks after the farmers in Switzerland. It pays **direct payments**, that is, contributions for services such as caring for the landscape, animal welfare and protecting the environment. In this way agriculture is meant to produce healthy food while also protecting nature. Rules for organic products and designations of origin are also among its topics.

**National economic supply** also belongs to the EAER. It makes sure that stocks of food, medicines and fuel are kept for crises. The Price Supervisor makes sure that prices are not unfairly high. The Federal Office for Housing and the Federal Office for Civilian Service also belong to the department.

begriffe.erklaerung: The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, the federal government's most important economic office.
Training in which you work in a company and also attend vocational school.
Money that the federal government pays farms for certain services.
The current state of the economy, whether it is growing or shrinking.

gewusst: For emergencies, Switzerland keeps compulsory stocks, for example of rice, sugar and coffee.
Many later Nobel Prize winners studied or worked at ETH Zurich, including Albert Einstein.
The Price Supervisor is a separate office that anyone can turn to with complaints about high prices.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Federal Office of Energy (SFOE, in German BFE) is the federal government's specialist authority for all questions about energy. It makes sure that Switzerland is supplied with energy that is secure, affordable and environmentally friendly. The SFOE is based in Ittigen near Bern.
wichtigste: The SFOE belongs to the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC).
It is based in Ittigen near Bern.
In May 2017 voters approved the Energy Strategy 2050, with a ban on new nuclear power stations.
The SFOE carries out this energy strategy.
In 2024 hydropower supplied about 60 per cent of the country's own electricity production.
With the SwissEnergy programme, the SFOE gives information about saving energy and renewable energy.
The SFOE also monitors the safety of large dams.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Federal Office of Energy** is an authority of the federal administration. It belongs to **DETEC**, the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications. It is based in Ittigen near Bern. The SFOE prepares laws and rules on energy and advises the Federal Council. It also collects figures on the production and use of energy in Switzerland.

In May 2017 Swiss voters approved the **Energy Strategy 2050**. It bans the building of new nuclear power stations and promotes renewable energy and saving energy. The SFOE is responsible for carrying out this strategy. This includes subsidies for solar installations and other renewable power stations. Another aim is that by 2050 Switzerland should no longer emit any greenhouse gases overall; this is called **net zero**.

Every year the SFOE publishes the **electricity statistics**. From these we know, for example, that in 2024 hydropower supplied about 60 per cent of the country's own electricity production. The second-largest share comes from nuclear power stations. Solar electricity is growing especially fast. In winter Switzerland often has to **import** electricity from abroad; in summer it often exports.

Through the **SwissEnergy** programme, the SFOE has given tips on saving energy and on renewable energy since 2001. It supports municipalities, companies and schools with projects. The SFOE is also responsible for the **energy label**, which shows on appliances and cars how economical they are. During the threatened energy shortage in winter 2022/23, the federal government called on people to save. Many people lowered the room temperature or switched off lights at that time.

The SFOE monitors the safety of large **dams** and reservoirs, for example the Grande Dixence. It is also involved in planning power lines and grids. In the search for a site for a **deep repository** for radioactive waste, the SFOE leads the process. The safety of the nuclear power stations themselves, however, is supervised by the independent ENSI. In this way several bodies share the responsibility.

begriffe.erklaerung: The Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications, to which the SFOE belongs.
Switzerland's plan for a secure and climate-friendly energy supply.
The aim of no longer emitting any additional greenhouse gases overall.
A coloured label that shows how much energy an appliance uses.

gewusst: Switzerland has more than 200 large dams, which are checked regularly.
In winter Switzerland needs more electricity than it produces itself and therefore often imports from neighbouring countries.
Every year the SFOE keeps statistics on how much energy Switzerland uses.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Civil Aviation, FOCA for short (in German BAZL), is the federal authority for everything that flies in Switzerland and does not belong to the military. It makes sure that aeroplanes, helicopters and drones travel safely. Airports and pilots are also under its supervision.
wichtigste: FOCA is the federal aviation authority and belongs to the department DETEC.
It is based in Ittigen near Bern.
Civil aviation means all flying that is not military.
FOCA monitors the safety of aircraft, airports and airlines.
It issues licences for pilots.
It also sets rules for drones.
For this, Switzerland works closely with the European Union Aviation Safety Agency EASA.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Civil Aviation** is the supervisory authority for civil aviation in Switzerland. **Civil** means that it is about passenger flights, cargo flights, rescue helicopters and sport pilots, not the air force. FOCA belongs to DETEC and is based in Ittigen near Bern. Its predecessor, the Federal Air Office, was founded as early as 1920.

Before an aircraft may fly in Switzerland, it must be approved and checked regularly. FOCA checks airlines, maintenance companies and flying schools. It also issues **licences** for pilots and air traffic controllers. Since 2006 Switzerland has taken part in the European Union Aviation Safety Agency **EASA**, so that similar rules apply everywhere in Europe.

The largest airports in Switzerland are Zurich and Geneva. Basel airport is on French soil and is run jointly by France and Switzerland. FOCA approves how airports are built and run. It also deals with **aircraft noise** and with rules on when flying is not allowed at night.

More and more people fly **drones**, for example to take photos from the air. FOCA decides where and how high drones may fly. Since 2023 largely the same drone rules have applied in Switzerland as in the EU. Anyone operating a drone weighing 250 grams or more, or one with a camera, must usually register.

FOCA works together with other bodies. Air navigation services, that is, guiding the aircraft in the sky, are provided by the company **Skyguide**. Air accidents are investigated by the independent Swiss Transportation Safety Investigation Board. FOCA also represents Switzerland in international aviation organisations.

begriffe.erklaerung: All flights that are not carried out by the military.
Official permission, for example to fly an aircraft.
Experts on the ground who make sure that aircraft pass each other safely.
A small remote-controlled aircraft with no people on board.

gewusst: EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse is in France but has its own Swiss customs area.
Hot-air balloons and gliders also belong to civil aviation.
Near airports, drones are usually not allowed to fly at all, or only with a permit.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, FDPIC for short (in German EDÖB), makes sure that personal data are protected in Switzerland. The Commissioner checks federal authorities and private companies. The FDPIC also helps citizens get access to documents of the administration.
wichtigste: The FDPIC monitors compliance with data protection at federal level.
The office is based in Bern and works independently.
It is based on the Data Protection Act (FADP), which has applied in revised form since 1 September 2023.
Personal data are all information about a particular person.
Health data are considered especially sensitive.
The FDPIC also mediates when someone asks to see official federal documents.
In the EU, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) has applied since 25 May 2018.

abschnitte.text: The **FDPIC** is an independent federal supervisory authority based in Bern. It has two tasks: data protection and the principle of transparency. Since 2023 the person at its head has been elected by the United Federal Assembly. In the cantons there are also separate data protection commissioners for cantonal authorities.

The **Data Protection Act**, FADP for short, regulates how personal data are handled in Switzerland. Since 1 September 2023 a renewed version has applied, adapted to the digital world. **Personal data** are all information about a particular person, for example name, address, photos or location. Health data or information about religion, for example, are especially sensitive.

The FDPIC checks whether companies and federal authorities follow the rules. The Commissioner can open investigations and, since 2023, can also issue binding orders. The FDPIC also advises people who want to know what data are stored about them. Anyone who suspects a breach of data protection can report it to the FDPIC.

On the internet, data are being collected all the time. **Cookies** are small text files in the browser that websites use, for example, to remember what you have looked at. When an app asks for **permission** to use the microphone, it wants to access it. Most big social networks require a minimum age of 13 in their terms of use.

Since 2006 the **principle of transparency** has applied in the federal administration. This means that, in principle, anyone may see official federal documents, unless there are important reasons against it. If an office refuses access, you can ask the FDPIC to mediate. In this way the Commissioner helps the state to work transparently.

begriffe.erklaerung: All information that belongs to a particular person.
Rules that prevent personal data from being misused.
The General Data Protection Regulation of the European Union.
The right to see documents of the administration.
A small text file that a website stores in your browser.

gewusst: You have the right to ask a company which data it has stored about you.
A photo in which you can be clearly recognised also counts as your personal data.
The first version of the Swiss Data Protection Act dates from 1992.

teile.einleitung: MeteoSwiss is the Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology, that is, Switzerland's national weather service. It measures the weather, makes the weather forecasts and warns of severe weather. It also watches how the climate in Switzerland is changing.
wichtigste: MeteoSwiss is the federal office responsible for weather forecasting in Switzerland.
It belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs.
Its headquarters is in Zurich, and there are other sites in Geneva, Locarno and Payerne.
A network of automatic measuring stations measures temperature, wind and precipitation round the clock.
MeteoSwiss warns the population of severe weather using five danger levels.
Since pre-industrial times, Switzerland has warmed about twice as much as the world on average (as of 2024).

abschnitte.text: MeteoSwiss is the official federal **weather service**. Its roots go back to 1881, when the Swiss Central Meteorological Institute was founded. Today experts in meteorology, computer science and physics work together. Their forecasts appear in the MeteoSwiss app, on the radio, on television and in newspapers.

The weather is observed at about 160 automatic **measuring stations** of the SwissMetNet network, from the lowlands up to high mountain peaks. Five **weather radars**, for example on the Albis and on Monte Lema, detect rain, snow and hail. In Payerne, weather balloons rise into the sky every day and measure the air up to great heights. In addition, there are data from satellites.

All the measurements go into **weather models** that run on supercomputers. The computers calculate how air pressure, temperature and humidity will change over the next hours and days. Then meteorologists check the results and produce the forecast. Because Switzerland has so many mountains and valleys, this is especially demanding.

For thunderstorms, gales, heavy rain, heat or black ice, MeteoSwiss issues **severe weather warnings**. There are five danger levels, from low to very great danger. The warnings go to the authorities, the fire brigade and the population. In this way people can protect themselves in good time, for example by putting cars under cover or postponing trips.

MeteoSwiss collects series of measurements, some of which go back to 1864. They show that Switzerland has become much warmer, about twice as much as the worldwide average. One reason is that land areas warm up faster than oceans. Together with ETH Zurich and other partners, MeteoSwiss produces **climate scenarios** that show how the climate could develop in future.

An important customer of MeteoSwiss is **aviation**. At Zurich and Geneva airports, experts watch the weather especially closely. Pilots need information about wind, fog, thunderstorms and icing. In this way flights can take off and land safely.

begriffe.erklaerung: The science of the weather.
The science of the climate, that is, the weather over many years.
A device that uses radio waves to detect rain and hail in the air.
A balloon that carries measuring instruments high into the air.

gewusst: On the Säntis the weather has been measured regularly since 1882.
A weather balloon from Payerne can rise more than 30 kilometres before it bursts.
The MeteoSwiss weather app is one of the most used apps in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Chancellery is the staff office of the Federal Council, something like its secretariat and planning centre. It prepares the government's meetings and makes sure that federal votes and elections are carried out correctly. It is headed by the Federal Chancellor.
wichtigste: The Federal Chancellery is the staff office of the Federal Council.
It is headed by the Federal Chancellor; since 2024 this has been Viktor Rossi.
The Federal Chancellor is elected by the United Federal Assembly.
The Federal Chancellery organises federal votes and elections.
It checks whether popular initiatives and referendums have enough valid signatures.
It publishes the federal laws.
The Swiss Federal Chancellor is not head of government like the Federal Chancellor in Germany.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Chancellery** is the staff office of the Swiss government. It plans and organises the weekly meetings of the Federal Council and writes down the decisions. It is one of the oldest federal authorities and goes back to 1803. It is based in the West Wing of the Federal Palace in Bern.

It is headed by the **Federal Chancellor**. Like the Federal Council, this person is elected by the United Federal Assembly, for four years. The Chancellor takes part in Federal Council meetings and may speak but not vote. Viktor Rossi has held this office since 2024; before him it was Walter Thurnherr.

The Federal Chancellery is responsible for **political rights**. Together with the cantons and municipalities, it organises federal votes and the National Council elections. It also publishes the voting booklet, in which the Federal Council explains the proposals. It is also testing electronic voting, so-called e-voting, with the cantons.

A **popular initiative** needs 100,000 valid signatures within 18 months. A referendum against a law needs 50,000 signatures in 100 days. The Federal Chancellery counts and checks these signatures and determines whether an initiative or a referendum has succeeded. Only then can the people vote on it.

The Federal Chancellery publishes all new laws and ordinances in the **Official Compilation**. This also includes the Federal Gazette and the Classified Compilation, where you can look up all the laws in force. The Vice-Chancellor is often the spokesperson of the Federal Council and informs the media. The Federal Chancellery also makes sure that texts exist in the official languages.

begriffe.erklaerung: An office that helps a leadership plan and organise its work.
A proposal from the people to change the Federal Constitution.
The right to have a vote on a law passed by Parliament.
A language in which the state writes officially; in Switzerland German, French, Italian and partly Romansh.

gewusst: The Federal Chancellor is sometimes called the eighth member of the Federal Council.
In 2000, Annemarie Huber-Hotz became the first woman to be Federal Chancellor.
In Germany the word Federal Chancellor has a quite different meaning: there it is the head of government.

teile.einleitung: Skyguide is Switzerland's air navigation service and makes sure that aircraft fly safely through Swiss airspace. Skyguide's air traffic controllers tell pilots when to take off and land and at what height to fly. The company belongs almost entirely to the federal government.
wichtigste: Skyguide monitors and directs air traffic in Swiss airspace.
The company belongs mostly to the federal government.
Its headquarters is in Geneva.
Large control centres are in Geneva and in Dübendorf near Zurich.
Skyguide is responsible for both civil and military air traffic.
Swiss airspace is small but lies right in the middle of Europe and is very busy.

abschnitte.text: Skyguide is an **air navigation services** company. This means it makes sure that aircraft keep enough distance from each other and do not collide. For this, the controllers watch all the aircraft on **radar**. By radio, they give pilots instructions, for example a new flight level or direction.

At airports, air traffic controllers sit in the **control tower** and see the runways right in front of them. They give permission to take off and land. As soon as an aircraft is in the air, the controllers in a large control centre take over. Skyguide runs such centres in Geneva and in Dübendorf near Zurich.

abschnitte.titel: An airspace in the middle of Europe
abschnitte.text: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe, so many flight routes cross here. That is why Skyguide monitors not only Switzerland but also some neighbouring parts of the airspace of nearby countries. An important goal is a single European airspace, which many countries are working on. Skyguide therefore works closely with the air navigation services of neighbouring countries.

In the past, air navigation was a task of federal offices and the company Radio Suisse. From this a separate company was formed, which has been called **Skyguide** since 2001. In 2002 two aircraft collided over Überlingen on Lake Constance while the airspace was being monitored by Skyguide. After this serious accident, procedures and safety technology were greatly improved.

abschnitte.titel: The job of air traffic controller
abschnitte.text: Air traffic controller is a demanding job that requires a lot of concentration. Training takes several years and partly takes place in a **simulator**. You must speak good English, because English is usually used on the radio with pilots. Quick thinking and a good sense of space are also important.

begriffe.erklaerung: Monitoring and directing air traffic so that nothing goes wrong.
A person who gives pilots instructions by radio.
A device that uses radio waves to locate aircraft in the sky.
The control tower at an airport.

gewusst: Controllers work even at night, when hardly any aircraft take off, because many aircraft fly over Switzerland.
On the radio with pilots, controllers use their own spelling alphabet with words such as Alpha, Bravo and Charlie.

teile.einleitung: Civil defence helps the population when a disaster or a major emergency happens in Switzerland. It is called out, for example, in floods, landslides, storms or large accidents. Civil defence also includes the shelters and the sirens, which you hear once a year in the siren test.
wichtigste: Civil defence protects and supports the population in disasters and emergencies.
It is part of civil protection, together with the police, fire brigade, ambulance service and technical services.
The cantons organise civil defence, and the federal government makes the rules.
Swiss men who do not do military service but are healthy enough often do protection service.
In Switzerland there is a place in a shelter for almost every inhabitant.
Every year on the first Wednesday in February the sirens are tested.

abschnitte.text: **Civil defence** is an organisation that helps people in emergencies. It is part of **civil protection**, a network of several partners. These include the police, the fire brigade, the health services, the technical services such as electricity and water, and civil defence itself. The police and fire brigade are usually first on the scene; civil defence supports them mainly in long and large operations.

After storms, members of civil defence clear away mud and rubble and build protective walls against floods. They look after people who have had to leave their homes and help out in hospitals or care homes. They also protect **cultural property**, that is, valuable buildings, pictures and documents. Sometimes they also help with traffic and logistics at large events such as sports festivals or anniversaries.

Switzerland has a special system: there is a place in a **shelter** for almost everyone. These rooms are usually in the basements of blocks of flats or in public buildings. They have thick concrete walls, heavy doors and ventilation with filters. They were built mainly during the Cold War, when people feared a war with nuclear weapons. Today many shelters are used as cellars or storerooms in everyday life.

There are sirens all over Switzerland to warn the population. For the **general alarm**, a wailing tone that rises and falls sounds. Then you should listen to the radio, check the Alertswiss app and follow the instructions of the authorities. Every year on the first Wednesday in February the **siren test** takes place, to make sure that all the sirens work.

In Switzerland men have a duty to serve. Those who are not fit for the army but are fit for civil defence do **protection service**. Women and foreign nationals can take part voluntarily. Members are trained in courses, for example as carers, pioneers or staff assistants. At federal level the responsible body is the Federal Office for Civil Protection, which belongs to the Department of Defence.

begriffe.erklaerung: Cooperation between the police, fire brigade, ambulance service, technical services and civil defence in emergencies.
A safe room made of thick concrete where people can find protection in danger.
A siren tone that means: switch on the radio and follow the instructions.
Measures to save valuable buildings, works of art and archives from destruction.

gewusst: Hardly any other country in the world has as many shelter places per inhabitant as Switzerland.
Some large shelter facilities are now used as emergency accommodation or even as rehearsal rooms for bands.

teile.einleitung: The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, SECO for short, is the federal specialist office for economic policy. It watches how the Swiss economy is doing, looks after the unemployed and negotiates trade agreements with other countries. Its work affects whether companies grow well and people find work.
wichtigste: SECO belongs to the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER).
It was created in 1999 from the Federal Office for Foreign Economic Affairs and the Federal Office for Economic Development and Labour.
SECO publishes the quarterly estimates of Swiss gross domestic product (GDP).
It is responsible for unemployment insurance and the unemployment figures.
It negotiates free trade agreements and carries out international sanctions.
It also deals with protecting employees, for example regarding working hours.

abschnitte.text: SECO is the federal **centre of expertise** for economic questions and is based in Bern. Its job is to make sure that Switzerland remains an attractive place for companies. At the same time it makes sure that employees are protected. It is headed by a State Secretary.

SECO watches the **state of the economy**, that is, whether the economy is growing or shrinking. Every quarter it estimates **gross domestic product**, the value of all goods and services produced in Switzerland. It also makes forecasts for the coming years. These figures are important for the Federal Council, the National Bank and companies.

Anyone who loses their job registers with the **Regional Employment Centre**, RAV for short. The RAVs are run by the cantons, but SECO manages unemployment insurance at federal level. Every month SECO publishes the unemployment rate. Together with the cantons, it also monitors the Labour Act, which regulates, for example, rest periods and the protection of young people.

Switzerland earns a lot of money from exports, for example of medicines, machines and watches. That is why SECO negotiates **free trade agreements**, often together with the other EFTA states. Examples are the agreement with China from 2014 and the EFTA agreement with India, which came into force in 2025. SECO also checks which sensitive goods may be exported, for example war material.

When the Federal Council decides to adopt economic **sanctions** against a country, SECO carries them out. Since 2022, for example, Switzerland has adopted many EU sanctions against Russia in this way. SECO also supports economic development in poorer countries, for example through better conditions for companies. In this way it complements the work of the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC).

begriffe.erklaerung: How the economy is doing, that is, whether it is growing or weakening at the moment.
The total value of all goods and services that a country produces in a certain period.
A treaty between countries that removes customs duties and other barriers to trade.
A punitive measure, for example a trade ban, against another country.

gewusst: SECO also measures consumer sentiment, that is, how optimistic people feel about their finances.
Together with EFTA, Switzerland has a network of more than 30 free trade agreements with countries all over the world.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Police, fedpol for short, is the federal police authority. It deals with serious crimes that go beyond one canton or across the national border, for example terrorism or organised crime. It also protects Federal Councillors and is responsible for the Swiss passport.
wichtigste: fedpol belongs to the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) and is based in Bern.
Most police work in Switzerland is done by the cantons; fedpol takes on cases of national importance.
The Federal Criminal Police investigate terrorism, organised crime, money laundering and counterfeit money.
fedpol protects members of the Federal Council, Parliament and foreign embassies.
It is the link to Interpol, Europol and police cooperation in the Schengen area.
fedpol is also responsible for Swiss identity documents such as the passport and identity card.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland, **police sovereignty** basically lies with the cantons. But some crimes are so big or so international that the federal government is responsible. For these there is the Federal Office of Police, which calls itself **fedpol**. It works closely with the cantonal police forces, the Office of the Attorney General and police authorities abroad.

The **Federal Criminal Police** carry out investigations on behalf of the Office of the Attorney General. They pursue, for example, terror suspects, criminal gangs, people traffickers and money launderers. Cases of counterfeit money and certain attacks on computers are also included. Often experts in computing, finance and policing work together on them.

fedpol looks after the safety of people who could be especially at risk. These include members of the **Federal Council**, members of Parliament and foreign state guests. Embassies and international organisations in Switzerland are also protected. At large events such as conferences in Geneva, fedpol helps with security planning.

Criminals do not stop at national borders, so international cooperation is very important. fedpol is Switzerland's link to **Interpol**, an organisation that connects police authorities from almost every country in the world. Through the Schengen Information System it exchanges wanted-person data with European countries. Switzerland also works with **Europol**, the EU's police agency.

fedpol is responsible for Swiss **identity documents**, that is, the passport and the identity card. It runs national databases, for example of fingerprints and DNA profiles, which help the cantons in investigations. The Money Laundering Reporting Office is also part of fedpol. Banks must report suspicious cases there when money might come from crime.

begriffe.erklaerung: The right to be in charge of the police; in Switzerland it usually lies with the cantons.
The federal prosecution service, which prosecutes serious crimes of national importance.
Hiding the fact that money comes from crime.
An international organisation that connects the police authorities of different countries.

gewusst: The name fedpol comes from the French word “fédéral” and the word police.
Unlike many other countries, Switzerland has no single national police force but 26 cantonal police forces plus fedpol.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for Agriculture, FOAG for short (in German BLW), looks after Swiss farms and their work. It makes sure that food is produced in Switzerland while nature is protected. For this it pays out billions of francs to farmers every year.
wichtigste: The FOAG belongs to the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER) and is based in Bern.
It carries out the federal government's agricultural policy.
Farms receive direct payments from the federal government for their services.
To receive direct payments, they must provide the proof of ecological performance (PEP).
Under the PEP, as a rule at least 7 per cent of the farmland must be biodiversity promotion areas.
The FOAG protects specialities such as Gruyère with the labels AOP and IGP.
The tasks of agriculture are set out in Article 104 of the Federal Constitution.

abschnitte.text: The FOAG is the federal specialist office for **agriculture**. It belongs to the EAER and works closely with the research institute Agroscope. It prepares laws and ordinances and pays money out to farms. Its basis is the Agriculture Act. According to the **Federal Constitution**, agriculture should supply the population with food, preserve nature, look after the landscape and help to keep even remote areas settled.

Swiss farms often could not survive from selling their products alone, because costs are high. That is why they receive **direct payments** from the federal government, about 2.8 billion francs a year in total. These pay for services to the community, for example looking after mountain meadows or especially animal-friendly stables. Those who do more for nature and animals get extra contributions. The FOAG sets the rules, and the cantons check the farms.

To receive direct payments, a farm must provide the **proof of ecological performance**, PEP for short. This includes keeping farm animals in a way that suits them and a balanced use of fertiliser. Fields must be farmed in a set crop rotation so that the soil stays healthy. As a rule, at least 7 per cent of the area must be **biodiversity promotion areas**, such as flower meadows, hedges or traditional orchards with tall fruit trees. There, insects, birds and other animals find a habitat.

The FOAG keeps a register of protected designations of origin. **AOP** marks a product that is made entirely in its region of origin, for example Gruyère, Emmentaler or Raclette du Valais. **IGP** means that at least one step of production takes place in the region, for example with Bündnerfleisch or the St Gallen bratwurst. This means others cannot simply copy these names. The FOAG also regulates what may be sold as organic.

To protect home-grown agriculture, Switzerland charges **customs duties** on many imported foods. The FOAG helps decide how much of a product may be imported at a lower duty. The number of farms has been falling for decades; in 2023 there were still about 48,000. At the same time, individual farms are getting bigger. Important questions for the future are climate change, fewer plant protection products and healthy soils.

begriffe.erklaerung: The rules and goals with which the state steers agriculture.
Money from the federal government to farms for services to nature and society.
The variety of animals, plants and habitats.
A protected designation of origin for products that come entirely from a particular region.

gewusst: Tall traditional fruit trees also count as a biodiversity promotion area, because many birds and insects live in them.
A large part of Switzerland's farmland is grassland, which is suited above all to cows, sheep and goats.
There are extra federal contributions for animals that are regularly allowed outdoors.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Department of Finance, FDF for short (in German EFD), is one of the seven departments of the federal administration. It looks after the federal government's money: taxes, spending, debts and customs. You can think of it as the finance department of the whole of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The FDF is one of seven departments and is headed by a member of the Federal Council.
Every year it plans the federal budget, that is, income and spending.
The Federal Tax Administration in the FDF collects, for example, value added tax and direct federal tax.
The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security also belongs to the FDF.
Since 2003 the debt brake has made sure that the federal government does not permanently spend more than it takes in.
One third of the National Bank's ordinary profit goes to the federal government and two thirds to the cantons.
The FDF's headquarters is the Bernerhof in Bern, right next to the Federal Palace.

abschnitte.text: The FDF makes sure that the federal government has enough **income** and spends the money sensibly. It prepares the **estimates**, that is, the budget, for the next year. The National Council and the Council of States then decide on it. At the end of the year, the FDF shows in the state accounts what the money was really used for.
