The FDF includes several offices with different tasks. The **Federal Tax Administration** deals with federal taxes, and the Federal Finance Administration with the budget and the accounts. The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security checks goods and people at the border. Other offices include the Federal Office of Information Technology and Telecommunications, the Federal Office for Buildings and Logistics and the State Secretariat for International Finance.

The federal government lives mainly on taxes. The most important source of income is **value added tax**, which is added to almost all purchases. Its standard rate has been 8.1 per cent since 2024. On top of this come direct federal tax on income and profits, withholding tax and charges on fuel and tobacco.

In 2001 Swiss voters approved the **debt brake** by a large majority. Since 2003 the rule has applied that, over a number of years, spending may not be higher than income. In bad economic years the federal government may spend more for a short time; in good years it has to save. In this way debts are not meant to keep on growing.

The Swiss National Bank is independent, but part of its profit goes to the public sector. The federal government and the National Bank agree on a **profit distribution** for this. One third goes to the federal government and two thirds to the cantons. In years when the National Bank makes big losses, however, this distribution can be cancelled completely.

At its head is a member of the Federal Council who deals with all financial questions. Since 2023 **Karin Keller-Sutter** has headed the department. In crises such as the rescue of the big bank Credit Suisse in 2023, the FDF played an important role. International tax and banking questions are also negotiated here.

begriffe.erklaerung: A plan of how much money you intend to take in and spend in the next year.
A tax included in the price when you shop, which goes to the federal government.
A rule that prevents the state from permanently spending more than it takes in.
A large part of the federal administration headed by a member of the Federal Council.

gewusst: In the 2001 vote, about 85 per cent of voters said yes to the debt brake.
The Federal Office for Buildings and Logistics in the FDF buys, among other things, office supplies and manages federal buildings, including embassies abroad.

teile.einleitung: The fire brigade puts out fires and rescues people and animals from dangerous situations. In Switzerland you can reach it on the emergency number 118. The vast majority of firefighters volunteer alongside their jobs.
wichtigste: In Switzerland you can reach the fire brigade on 118.
The European emergency number 112 also works in Switzerland.
Most fire brigades are militia fire brigades, whose members take part voluntarily alongside their jobs.
Large cities such as Zurich, Basel, Bern, Geneva and Lausanne also have professional fire brigades.
The fire brigade does not only put out fires but also helps with accidents, storms and chemical accidents.
Fire brigades are organised and paid for by the municipalities and cantons, that is, with taxes and charges.

abschnitte.text: The fire brigade has four main tasks: **rescuing**, extinguishing, protecting and recovering. It gets people out of burning houses, out of cars after accidents or out of flooded cellars. In thunderstorms and floods it pumps away water and clears fallen trees. Specialised groups deal with oil, chemicals or radiation.

There are about 1300 fire brigades in Switzerland, most of them **militia fire brigades**. Their members have a normal job and turn out when their pager or phone raises the alarm. Large cities also have **professional fire brigades**, which are ready at the station round the clock. In many municipalities you have to pay a substitute charge if you do not do fire brigade service.

Anyone who notices a fire should call **118** straight away. The call is free and goes to an emergency control centre. There, experts ask what has happened, where the fire is and whether people are in danger. It is very important to get yourself to safety and never to go back into a burning house.

Many fires are caused by candles, hotplates, faulty appliances or cigarettes. In Switzerland the cantonal **building insurance companies** and the fire brigades look after fire protection. **Smoke alarms** give an early warning with a loud sound when there is a fire in the flat. A small fire extinguisher or a fire blanket in the kitchen can help to smother a fire quickly.

Anyone interested in the fire brigade can join the **youth fire brigade** in many municipalities. There, children and young people learn in a playful way how to lay hoses, handle water and work as a team. Later they can move on to the active fire brigade. In this way the fire brigades make sure they have new recruits.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fire brigade whose members volunteer alongside their jobs.
A fire brigade with professionals who work all day at the station.
A small device on the ceiling that beeps loudly when there is smoke.
Equipment with an air cylinder and mask so that firefighters can breathe in smoke.

gewusst: Firefighters must be able to work wearing heavy breathing apparatus weighing more than 15 kilograms.
In fires, the poisonous smoke is often more dangerous than the flames themselves.
For worries of any kind, children and young people in Switzerland can call Pro Juventute's helpline on 147.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Patent Court is a federal court that deals only with disputes about patents. A patent protects an invention so that nobody may simply copy it. The court is based in St Gallen and has existed since 2012.
wichtigste: The Federal Patent Court is Switzerland's court for disputes about patents.
It is based in St Gallen.
It began its work on 1 January 2012.
A patent protects a technical invention for at most 20 years.
Lawyers and technical experts work at the court.
Its judgements can be challenged at the Federal Supreme Court.
Patents themselves are granted by the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property in Bern.

abschnitte.text: A **patent** is a protective right for a new technical invention. Whoever holds a patent may decide who is allowed to make or sell the invention. To get one, the invention must be new and must not simply be obvious. The protection lasts at most 20 years; after that everyone may use the invention.

The **Federal Patent Court** has existed since 1 January 2012. It is based in the city of St Gallen in eastern Switzerland. In the past, the cantonal courts decided on patent disputes. Because these cases are often very technical and complicated, the federal government created a specialised court for the whole of Switzerland.

What is special is that not only lawyers judge here. There are also **technical judges** with a technical education, for example in chemistry, mechanical engineering or electrical engineering. Only a few judges work full-time at the court; most work **part-time**. In this way the right expertise can be put together for each case.

Typical cases are lawsuits because someone is said to have copied a protected invention. It can also be about whether a patent is valid at all. Often the companies involved are from the pharmaceutical industry, medical technology or mechanical engineering. A judgement can be appealed to the **Federal Supreme Court** in Lausanne.

Switzerland is a country of many inventions and files an especially large number of patents for the size of its population. Many large pharmaceutical and technology companies have their headquarters here. A fast and expert patent court is therefore important for the economy. However, the patents themselves are not granted by the court but by the **Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property** in Bern.

begriffe.erklaerung: A right that protects an invention from being copied for a certain time.
Rights to ideas and works, for example to inventions, brands or books.
A task that someone does in addition to their main job.
A request to a court to decide a dispute.

gewusst: Albert Einstein worked for several years at the patent office in Bern, where he examined inventions.
The Federal Patent Court is one of the smallest federal courts.
A patent only applies in the countries where it has been registered.

teile.einleitung: Rega is the Swiss Air-Rescue, that is, Switzerland's air rescue service. With helicopters and air ambulances, it helps people in need, for example after an accident in the mountains. You can call it out on the number 1414.
wichtigste: Rega is the Swiss air rescue service and is called out on the number 1414.
It was founded in 1952.
Rega is a non-profit foundation and is financed mainly by patrons.
Its helicopters are stationed at bases all over Switzerland.
With air ambulance jets, Rega brings sick or injured people back from abroad.
The operations centre is in the Rega Centre at Zurich Airport.
Rega is ready for action round the clock on every day of the year.

abschnitte.text: Rega brings medical help from the air. Its **helicopters** fly to accidents in the mountains, on roads or on lakes and take injured people quickly to hospital. On board there is always a pilot, an emergency doctor and a paramedic. In this way treatment starts at the scene of the accident.

Rega was founded on 27 April 1952 as the **Swiss Air-Rescue**. At first, rescuers even jumped with parachutes to reach injured people. Soon helicopters were used, which could help much faster and more safely. Today Rega is one of the best-known organisations in Switzerland.

Rega has helicopters at more than a dozen **bases** spread all over Switzerland. This means a helicopter can reach almost any place in the country in about 15 minutes' flying time. For the mountains it uses AgustaWestland AW109 helicopters, which can also fly at great altitude. There are also three **air ambulance jets**, with which patients are flown back to Switzerland from all over the world.

Many missions take place in the Alps, for example after skiing, climbing or hiking accidents. Where the helicopter cannot land, a rescuer is lowered on a rope with the **rescue winch**. Rega works closely with mountain rescuers of the Swiss Alpine Club. Sometimes cows or other animals are also recovered when they get into trouble.

Rega is a **non-profit foundation** and gets no money from the state for its operations. It lives mainly on contributions from its patrons, of whom there are more than three million. Patrons often do not have to pay anything if the costs of a mission are not covered by an insurance company. That is why many families in Switzerland are Rega patrons.

In Switzerland you dial **1414**; from abroad the number is +41 333 333 333. There is also the iRega app, which automatically sends your exact location when you raise the alarm. This helps especially in the mountains, where it is often hard to describe where you are. The operations centre then sends out the nearest free helicopter.

begriffe.erklaerung: Rescuing sick or injured people with helicopters or aircraft.
A motorised rope on the helicopter on which rescuers are lowered.
A person who donates money every year to support Rega.
An aircraft fitted out like a flying hospital.
An organisation that pursues a particular aim and does not seek to make a profit.

gewusst: In the early years, Rega rescuers jumped with parachutes to reach injured people.
Rega helicopters are easy to recognise by their red and white colours and the large Rega lettering.
Rega also flies sick people back to Switzerland from distant countries such as Thailand or Brazil.

teile.einleitung: Emergency numbers are short telephone numbers you can use to get help quickly in an emergency. In Switzerland there are separate numbers for the police, the fire brigade, the ambulance service and other emergencies. If you know them by heart, you can save lives when it really matters.
wichtigste: In Switzerland you can reach the police on 117.
If there is a fire, call the fire brigade on 118.
For an ambulance, call 144.
In a case of poisoning, Tox Info Suisse helps on 145.
Rega, the Swiss air rescue service, is called on 1414.
The number 112 works all over Europe and also in Switzerland.
Children and young people with worries can reach someone to talk to on 147.
Emergency numbers are free, and you may only dial them in an emergency.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland each emergency service has its own **emergency number**. 117 connects you with the police, 118 with the fire brigade and 144 with the ambulance service. 1414 calls out Rega, which also flies into the mountains with helicopters. On 145 you get advice about poisoning, for example if a small child has drunk a cleaning product. **112** is the European emergency number and in Switzerland also puts you through to the police.

abschnitte.titel: How to make an emergency call
abschnitte.text: Stay calm and speak slowly and clearly. It is best to answer the **key questions**: Who is calling? Where did it happen? What happened? How many people are injured? Do not hang up yourself, but wait until the person in the **emergency control centre** ends the call, because they may have more questions.

An emergency is when people, animals or property are in danger and help is needed quickly. Examples are a fire, an accident, an unconscious person or a bite from an adder. After a **snake bite**, stay calm, keep the part of the body still and dial 144. Anyone who makes an emergency call for fun blocks the line for real emergencies and can be punished for it.

Not every emergency needs blue lights. On Pro Juventute's number **147**, children and young people can talk about their worries for free round the clock, also by chat or text message. Adults can find someone to listen at the Dargebotene Hand helpline on 143. The conversations are confidential, which means nobody finds out about them without your permission.

You can also get into difficult situations online. If you see something on the internet that frightens you, tell an adult you **trust**. If someone is put down again and again in a group chat, this is called **cyberbullying**. Then it makes sense to take screenshots as evidence, to block or report the person and to involve someone you trust.

Emergency calls go to **control centres**, which are usually run by the cantons. Specially trained experts work there and send out the right emergency services. If you call with a mobile phone, the centre can often see your approximate location automatically. Even so, it is important to describe the place as precisely as possible.

begriffe.erklaerung: A call with which you get help straight away in a dangerous situation.
A place where experts take emergency calls and send out helpers.
Who, where, what, how many: these questions help you report an emergency clearly.
The rescue service with ambulances.
When someone is repeatedly picked on or shown up on the internet or in a chat.

gewusst: In Switzerland you can call emergency numbers free of charge, even from a phone box.
Fire engines in Switzerland often have the number 118 printed on them in large figures.
The number 112 works in all countries of the European Union and in many other countries.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Assembly is the parliament of Switzerland. It has two chambers, the National Council and the Council of States, and makes the laws for the whole country. When both chambers meet together, it is called the United Federal Assembly.
wichtigste: The Federal Assembly is the parliament and so the legislature of Switzerland.
It consists of the National Council with 200 members and the Council of States with 46 members.
Together they form the United Federal Assembly with 246 members.
The United Federal Assembly elects the Federal Council and the federal judges.
Every year it elects one member of the Federal Council as President of the Confederation.
On 16 November 1848 the Federal Assembly elected the first Federal Council.
On 28 November 1848 it chose Bern as the seat of the federal authorities.

abschnitte.text: The Swiss parliament has two equally important chambers. The **National Council** represents the people and has 200 seats, which are shared out among the cantons according to population. The **Council of States** represents the cantons; each canton has two seats and the six half-cantons one each, making 46 in all. A law only comes into force if both chambers agree.

The Federal Assembly is the **legislature**, that is, the law-making power. It debates and passes laws and decides on the federal budget. It supervises the Federal Council and the administration. With a motion it can oblige the Federal Council to prepare a new law.

For elections, the National Council and the Council of States meet in the National Council chamber. This joint session is called the **United Federal Assembly** and has 246 members. It elects the seven members of the Federal Council, the Federal Chancellor and the judges of the Federal Supreme Court. Every year it also elects the President of the Confederation from among the members of the Federal Council.

The Federal Assembly was created with the **Federal Constitution of 1848**. On 16 November 1848 it elected the first Federal Council. Shortly afterwards, on 28 November 1848, it chose Bern as the seat of the federal authorities. Today's parliament building, the Federal Palace, was opened in 1902.

Members of parliament are elected by the people every four years. The councils meet four times a year for a three-week **session** in Bern. Many members have another job besides politics, for example as a farmer, teacher or businesswoman. That is why it is called a **militia parliament**.

begriffe.erklaerung: The law-making power, that is, parliament.
A part of parliament that debates and votes separately.
The period in which parliament meets and debates.
Political offices are carried out alongside a normal job.

gewusst: In the National Council the canton of Zurich has the most seats, while small cantons such as Uri have only one.
When parliament votes today, members press buttons and the result appears on a large board.
If there is room in the public gallery, visitors may also watch sessions in the Federal Palace.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Justice (FOJ, in German BJ) is the federal government's legal department. It helps to draft new laws, assists in cooperation with foreign authorities and keeps important registers. The FOJ is based in Bern.
wichtigste: The FOJ belongs to the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
It prepares laws, for example in civil law, criminal law and constitutional law.
It checks whether new laws are compatible with the Federal Constitution.
The FOJ is responsible for international legal assistance and extraditions.
It keeps Switzerland's criminal record register.
The FOJ supervises the commercial register, in which companies are entered.
It helps with international child abductions and adoptions.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Justice** is a federal authority based in Bern. It belongs to the **Federal Department of Justice and Police** (FDJP). You can think of it as the federal government's legal specialist office. Its lawyers advise the Federal Council and the other federal offices on legal questions. The FOJ is not a court and does not pass judgements.

An important task of the FOJ is **legislation**. It drafts new laws or changes, for example in the **Civil Code** or the **Criminal Code**. It also checks whether the laws are compatible with the Federal Constitution and international law. The drafts then go out for consultation, where cantons, parties and associations give their views. In the end the Federal Council and Parliament decide, and sometimes the people.

Criminals do not stop at national borders. That is why the FOJ works with foreign authorities on **international legal assistance**. For example, it decides on **extraditions** of wanted persons. It also helps to exchange evidence or stolen money between countries. In cases of children being abducted abroad, the FOJ is Switzerland's central point of contact.

The FOJ keeps the Swiss **criminal record register**, in which convictions are entered. Anyone starting a job working with children, for example, sometimes has to show an extract from it. The FOJ also supervises the **commercial register**, in which all the companies in Switzerland are listed. It also regulates civil status matters, where births, marriages and deaths are recorded. These registers ensure order and legal certainty.

The FOJ is the central authority for **international adoptions** and checks that the rights of the child are respected. It supports victims of crime with rules on victim support. The federal government also pays contributions through the FOJ for building prisons and for measures for young people. It also follows how the law develops in other countries. In this way the FOJ helps the **rule of law** to work well.
